systems.name: Chassis
systems.summary: The Gen 6 Camaro is a steel unibody (GM Alpha-derived) with bolt-on front and rear suspension cradles. GM quotes the coupe body as 28% stiffer and 133 lb lighter than Gen 5. A road-race build starts from a stripped coupe shell that is measured, stitch welded at critical seams, reinforced at cradle and cage mounting points, re-sealed and painted before lines, suspension and drivetrain are installed.
systems.overview:
The body-in-white carries all loads: the front cradle (engine, front lower control arms, radius rods, steering rack, front sway bar) bolts up into the two front frame rails; the MacPherson struts load the front strut towers directly; the rear cradle (differential, all five rear links, rear sway bar) bolts to the rear rails through four isolating bushings and is braced fore and aft by bolted cradle braces; the rear shocks load the rear shock pads while the rear coil springs react against body spring seats above the rear lower control arms.

For racing, the main structural tasks are: (1) measure the shell against GM underbody dimension data and record cradle-mount and strut-tower positions; (2) strip deadener/sealer at the seams to be welded; (3) stitch weld the strut towers, front rail flanges, floor-to-rocker, tunnel and rear rail/shock tower seams; (4) add doubler plates at cradle mounts (especially if cradles will be solid-mounted) and at all cage feet; (5) integrate the roll cage into towers, pillars and rockers where the rules allow; (6) re-seal, prime, paint and cavity-wax the shell.

Rules: NASA CCR and SCCA GCR control cage design, plate sizes, tow-point requirements, fuel-cell bulkheads and (by class) what seam welding or cage tie-ins are allowed - read the class rules before cutting or welding. Common failure points on hard-driven Gen 6 cars are cracked paint/seams at the strut towers, spun captured nuts at cradle mounts, and crushed rocker pinch welds from careless jacking.

All cradle and many suspension fasteners on this platform are torque-to-yield (torque + angle) and single-use per GM; chase every captured nut and plan on new fasteners for final assembly.
buildNotes: Buy/choose a coupe shell; verify VIN plates/documentation for registration and tech.
Mount on rotisserie/jig using cradle mounting points; record baseline measurements (cradle diagonals, tower-to-tower, rear shock pad positions).
Strip interior, deadener, sealer at weld zones; remove all lines and harnesses.
Stitch weld front structure, underbody and rear structure in a skip pattern; re-measure.
Weld cradle-mount doublers, strut tower reinforcements, jacking points, tabs, and cage landing plates; fit the cage (safety system).
Chase all captured nuts; install rivnuts along planned line/harness routes.
Epoxy prime, seam seal, paint, cavity wax, light chip coating; mask datum holes and ground pads.
Proceed to phase 2 (fuel cell, hard lines) then phase 3 (cradles, suspension, steering).

subsystems.name: Corrosion Protection & Coatings
subsystems.description: Stripping of factory sound deadener, undercoating and sealer where needed, then re-sealing seams, priming, painting and cavity protection after welding so the race shell does not rust from the inside.

subsystems.name: Floor & Transmission/Driveshaft Tunnel
subsystems.description: The central tunnel housing the transmission tail, driveshaft and exhaust, its bolt-on underbody brace, driveshaft safety loop, body plugs and tunnel heat protection.

subsystems.name: Mounting Points (Lift, Tow, Rivnuts, Tabs)
subsystems.description: Body hard points used for lifting/jacking, towing/recovery, and attaching lines, harnesses and small brackets: factory pinch-weld lift points, tow-eye receptacles, plus rivnuts and weld-on tabs added during the build.

subsystems.name: Seam Welding & Structural Reinforcement
subsystems.description: Stitch/seam welding of factory spot-welded seams and local reinforcement plates at high-load hard points (strut towers, cradle mounts, cage feet). Done on the bare shell before cage installation and paint.

subsystems.name: Unibody (Body-in-White)
subsystems.description: The bare steel Gen 6 (GM Alpha-derived) unibody shell as delivered for the build: floor pan, rockers, front and rear rails, strut/shock towers, dash panel, pillars, roof and trunk floor. Every suspension, drivetrain and safety load ultimately ends here, so it is measured, stripped, repaired and reinforced before anything is bolted on.

subsystems.name: Strut Tower & Chassis Braces
subsystems.description: Bolt-on braces tying the front strut towers together and the rear shock towers together. (Cradle braces are listed with the cradles under suspension.front-cradle / suspension.rear-cradle; the tunnel brace is under chassis.floor-and-tunnel.)

systems.name: Safety & Roll Cage
systems.summary: Driver protection for a bare-chassis Gen 6 Camaro road-race car: a weld-in 1.75 x .120 DOM roll cage tied into the unibody, FIA/SFI fixed-back seat, 6-point harness with FHR-compatible geometry, SFI 27.1 window net, plumbed Novec fire system plus hand-held extinguisher, external kill/fire pulls, sealed fuel-cell and engine firewalls, and marked tow points. The production car has none of this; every item is a race addition built to NASA CCR / SCCA GCR (and FIA App. J 253 where applicable).
systems.overview:
The cage is the structural and safety core of the car. A Gen 6 Camaro races at roughly 3,400–3,700 lb without driver and fuel, putting it in NASA's 3,001–4,000 lb tube bracket (1.75 x .120 DOM or chromoly, no ERW) as quoted from the CCR; SCCA's 2,700 lb+ table allows 1.50 x .120, 1.75 x .095 or 2.00 x .080 (no mixing alloy and mild steel, inspection holes in front/main hoop and one brace). FIA 253-8 (2020) build-to-spec uses 45 x 2.5 or 50 x 2.0 mm for the main hoop and 38 x 2.5 / 40 x 2.0 mm elsewhere, ≥3 mm/120 cm² reinforcement plates, and U-gussets ≥1 mm thick whose legs end 2–4 x OD from the junction.

Build sequence matters: strip and seam-weld the shell, mock up seat, steering column and pedals, then set hoop positions around the seated driver in full gear. The harness bar height is set from the seated driver so shoulder belts leave the shoulders at 0° to −20° (Schroth/FIA guidance; never upward with an FHR), and the seat back sits within ~200 mm of the bar. Lap belts anchor at 20°–70° on 7/16-20 eyebolts (40 N·m per Schroth) into ≥40 cm² x 3 mm plates; belts may never anchor to the seat or seat mounts.

Fire: a 10 lb SFI 17.1 or FIA-listed Novec 1230 system with 2 cockpit nozzles under the dash (aimed at footwell/midriff, never the face) and 3 engine-bay nozzles between mid-height and top of the engine. Tubing is the maker's homologated semi-rigid alloy tube with push-in fittings, P-clipped 75–100 mm behind every nozzle. Systems are recertified every 2 years by the maker only. Electrical cutoff hardware belongs to the electrical system; this system owns the mechanical pull cables, markings and decals.

Common failure points: expired belts/nets/seats (SFI belts and nets 2 years; FIA belts and 8855-1999 seats 5 years; 8862/8855-2021 seats 10 years), cracked floor around cage plates, padding slid off the helmet zone, loose seat bolts, bottle out of service date, and unsealed bulkhead pass-throughs letting fuel vapor into the cockpit.
buildNotes: Strip interior to bare shell; remove SRS/airbags and factory belts (interior.strip-and-deadener-removal).
Mock up seat, steering column, pedal box and driver in full gear before designing the cage.
Weld mounting plates, then main hoop, front hoop, roof rails, roof X, diagonals, harness bar, backstays, door bars, dash bar, optional front down-bars; gusset junctions.
Drill inspection holes, weld all tabs (seat brace, window net rods, dash, fire bottle, extinguisher) BEFORE paint/powder coat.
Install bulkheads (rear fuel-cell firewall, package shelf, front block-offs) and seal every pass-through.
Install seat mounts + reinforcement plates, harness anchors and plates; fit seat and harness; verify belt angles with driver.
Install fire system bottle/bracket, tubing, nozzles, pull cables; hand-held extinguisher; kill-switch pull cable.
Fit SFI 45.1 padding, window net, decals and tow straps last; record all expiry dates in the logbook.

subsystems.name: Fuel & Firewall Isolation
subsystems.description: Sheet-metal bulkheads that seal the cockpit from the trunk-mounted fuel cell and from the engine bay: rear bulkhead, package-shelf panel, sealed pass-throughs, and front firewall block-off plates.

subsystems.name: Harness
subsystems.description: 6-point racing harness (SFI 16.1/16.5 or FIA 8853-2016) with shoulder belts wrapped on the cage harness bar, lap and dual anti-sub belts on floor eyebolts with FIA-size reinforcement plates.

subsystems.name: Roll Cage
subsystems.description: Weld-in 6-point+ road-race roll cage (main hoop, front hoop, halo/roof rails, roof X, diagonals, harness bar, backstays, door bars, dash bar, optional strut-tower down-bars) with mounting plates, gussets and SFI 45.1 padding. Tube size per NASA CCR/SCCA GCR weight tables (1.75 x .120 DOM for a ~3,500 lb Camaro).

subsystems.name: Seat & Seat Mounts
subsystems.description: Fixed-back FIA/SFI racing seat on seat-specific side brackets, bolted to a welded floor mount / reinforcement plates, with optional rear seat-back brace to the harness bar.

subsystems.name: Window Net
subsystems.description: SFI 27.1 driver window net mounted inside the cage between the roof rail and door bars, with a spring-loaded top rod and quick-release latch the belted driver can operate.

subsystems.name: Fire Suppression System
subsystems.description: Plumbed on-board fire system (SFI 17.1 or FIA-listed, Novec 1230 / FK-5-1-12) with bottle on the passenger floor, semi-rigid alloy distribution tubing, 2 cockpit + 3 engine-bay nozzles, and mechanical pull cables inside and outside the car (electric actuation optional).

subsystems.name: Hand-Held Extinguisher
subsystems.description: Driver-reachable hand-held extinguisher on a metal quick-release mount (often required in addition to, or instead of, a plumbed system depending on series).

subsystems.name: Head & Neck Restraint Interface
subsystems.description: Car-side interface for the driver frontal head restraint (FHR): helmet anchors, FHR-compatible belt geometry, and seat/cage head surround padding. Driver personal gear is noted only where it affects installation.

subsystems.name: Kill Switch Pull Cable (Mechanical Side)
subsystems.description: External T-handle and pull cable that operate the master electrical cutoff from outside the car, plus markings. Switch, isolator and wiring are in electrical.battery-and-cutoff.

subsystems.name: Tow Hooks / Straps
subsystems.description: Front and rear tow points that recovery crews can reach without removing body parts, painted/marked in contrasting color.

systems.name: Suspension
systems.summary: Gen 6 Camaro uses a double-pivot (dual lower ball joint) MacPherson strut front with aluminum lateral LCA and forward radius rod, and a five-link independent rear with stamped steel links, the coil spring and shock both on the rear lower control arm. ZL1 runs Magnetic Ride Control; ZL1 1LE runs Multimatic DSSV dampers with adjustable front ride height, rotatable camber top mounts and a 3-way rear bar. Race builds solid-mount the cradles, replace rubber bushings with spherical bearings, add camber/caster plates and adjustable links, and fit adjustable coilovers.
systems.overview:
Front: each front corner has a MacPherson strut clamped to the knuckle (2 bolts, 150 N·m + 80-95 deg) and bolted to the tower (3 bolts, 22 N·m). The lower knuckle is located by two separate aluminum links with their own ball joints - a lateral lower control arm and a forward-running radius rod (tension/caster rod) - both pivoting on the front cradle with torque-to-yield bolts (100 N·m + 90-105 deg, GM P/N 11611268 LCA, 11610915 radius rod). Steering is a ZF rack-mounted electric rack on the front cradle. A direct-acting sway bar on the front of the cradle links to the strut bodies.

Rear: five links per side - lower control arm (spring link: carries the spring and the shock; M14 camber eccentric inside), upper control arm, upper and lower trailing arms, and a toe link (GM 'adjust link', M12 toe eccentric inside) - all pivot on a steel rear cradle that mounts to the body through four bushings with TTY bolts (100 N·m + 90-105 deg) and is braced front and rear. Almost every rear pivot fastener is torque + angle and single-use per GM (BMR publishes the GM fastener P/N list).

Race approach: (1) solid or Delrin cradle mounts (BMR BK062/BK063) and seam-welded cradle; (2) spherical bearings in all link bushings or rod-end links (BMR, SPL Parts); (3) camber/caster plates (BMR WAK360/361) and adjustable radius rods/LCAs (SPL TR CAM6, SPL FLCA CAM6, BMR FLC363) for -3 deg camber and equal caster; (4) adjustable rear links/lockouts (SPL EL CAM6, BMR TR007) so eccentrics cannot slip; (5) adjustable coilovers or retain DSSV; (6) adjustable bars and end links; (7) bump-steer tie rod ends (SPL TRE CAM6) when lowered.

Typical race alignment starting points: front camber -2.7 to -3.5 deg, caster 7.5-9 deg (equal L/R), front toe 0 to 1/16 in out; rear camber -1.5 to -2.2 deg, rear toe 1/16-1/8 in total in. Typical spring rates (estimate): front coilover 600-1000 lb/in; rear depends on layout (factory pocket spring has a low motion ratio). Rules: NASA/SCCA classes restrict suspension changes by class (e.g. ST/TT/GT classes use points/power-to-weight; SCCA T1/T2 and NASA AmEx/ST classes differ) - check class rules before buying parts.

Common failure points: OE rear eccentrics slipping (toe/camber change), worn radius rod bushings (braking instability), cracked strut tower seams, bent aluminum front links after curbing, and bushings torqued at full droop.
buildNotes: Rebuild/upgrade bushings and press bearings into links and knuckles on the bench before installation.
Assemble front cradle with rack, sway bar, LCAs and radius rods; install cradle (with engine if doing a K-member drop-in) using new TTY bolts.
Assemble struts (spring compressor), install struts and knuckles; leave all rubber-bushed TTY pivots loose.
Assemble rear cradle with differential, five links, sway bar; raise and bolt in; install braces; then springs and shocks.
Install hubs/brakes (phases 4) and wheels; set car on pads at ride height with ballast.
Final-torque all TTY pivots at ride height with new bolts; paint-mark.
Corner weight, then align (front camber/caster/toe, rear camber/toe); lock eccentrics; set sway bar links for zero preload.
Shakedown: re-torque top mounts, check witness marks, zip-tie damper shafts for travel.

subsystems.name: Bump Stops, Packers & Droop Limiters
subsystems.description: Jounce bumpers on the front strut and rear shock shafts, packers/spacers that set when the bump stop engages, and droop limiters. On a lowered race car the bump stop is a tuning element (it is effectively a rising-rate spring), not just a crash stop.

subsystems.name: Front Cradle (Front Subframe)
subsystems.description: The bolt-in front subframe that carries the engine mounts, both front lower links (lateral LCA and forward radius/tension rod), the ZF electric steering rack and the front sway bar, and bolts up into the front frame rails. ZL1 adds an aluminum lower cradle brace beneath it.

subsystems.name: Front Knuckles (Steering Knuckle / Upright)
subsystems.description: Front uprights that carry the hub bearing (wheels system), brake caliper (brakes system) and wheel speed sensor; clamp to the strut at the top; and take two lower ball joints plus the outer tie rod.

subsystems.name: Front Lower Links (Lateral LCA + Radius/Tension Rod)
subsystems.description: The Gen 6 front is a double-pivot MacPherson strut: instead of one lower A-arm, two separate aluminum links each carry their own ball joint at the knuckle. The lateral 'lower control arm' reacts mainly side loads; the forward-running 'radius rod' (GM: front lower control link; aftermarket: tension rod / caster rod) reacts braking/longitudinal loads and sets caster. Both inner pivots bolt to the front cradle with torque-to-yield bolts.

subsystems.name: Front Struts, Springs & Top Mounts
subsystems.description: Front MacPherson strut assemblies: damper (MRC on ZL1, Multimatic DSSV on ZL1 1LE/SS 1LE, conventional on SS), coil spring, spring seats/insulators, top mount, and race alternatives (coilovers, camber/caster plates, helper springs). The strut clamps to the knuckle with two torque-angle bolts and bolts to the tower with three bolts.

subsystems.name: Front Sway Bar (Stabilizer Shaft)
subsystems.description: Direct-acting front stabilizer bar mounted to the front of the cradle in two insulators/clamps, with end links running to brackets on the strut bodies. Race options are stiffer adjustable bars and adjustable spherical end links for preload-free installation.

subsystems.name: Rear Cradle (Rear Suspension Bracket / Subframe)
subsystems.description: Steel rear subframe carrying the differential, all inner pivots of the five rear links and the rear sway bar. It mounts to the body through four rubber bushings with torque-to-yield bolts and is braced by bolted front and rear cradle braces. Bushing compliance here lets the whole rear axle steer and squat; race cars use solid or Delrin mounts.

subsystems.name: Rear Five-Link Suspension Links
subsystems.description: The Gen 6 rear is a 5-link independent: per side a lower control arm (spring link, also carries the shock), an upper control arm (upper lateral/camber link), an upper trailing arm, a lower trailing arm (traction link) and a toe link (GM 'adjust link'). GM uses stamped steel links with lightening holes. Camber is adjusted with an eccentric cam bolt at the LCA inner pivot and toe with an eccentric at the toe-link inner pivot. Nearly every rear link fastener is torque-to-yield (torque + angle) per GM.

subsystems.name: Rear Knuckles (Rear Uprights / Spindles)
subsystems.description: Rear uprights carrying the hub bearing (wheels), caliper and electric parking brake (brakes), halfshaft (drivetrain) and wheel speed sensor, with pickup points for all five links and the rear sway bar end link.

subsystems.name: Rear Shocks & Springs
subsystems.description: Factory rear uses a separate coil spring seated in the lower control arm pocket and a shock mounted from the LCA to the body shock pad (3 nuts). ZL1 = MRC monotube; ZL1 1LE = Multimatic DSSV (hard-mounted, auto vs manual specific tune). Race option: keep the split spring/shock layout with race shocks and springs, or convert to rear coilovers with coilover-specific LCAs.

subsystems.name: Rear Sway Bar
subsystems.description: Rear stabilizer bar clamped to the rear cradle with end links down to the rear knuckles. ZL1 1LE has a three-position adjustable bar. Race options: adjustable bars and spherical end links.

subsystems.name: Ride Height / Position Sensors (Magnetic Ride Control)
subsystems.description: Cars with Magnetic Ride Control (ZL1, optional SS) use corner position sensors and a suspension control module to command the magnetorheological dampers. A race car with passive dampers deletes them; the same mounting points can be reused for data-acquisition linear potentiometers.

subsystems.name: Alignment, Ride Height & Corner-Weight Setup
subsystems.description: Setup targets and procedures performed at phase 11: ride height, corner weights, final torque of all rubber-bushed TTY pivots at ride height, and four-wheel alignment. Factory values are approximate (GM alignment specs by RPO are in GM SI and the Chevrolet Camaro Track Preparation Guide); race values are typical starting points for a Gen 6 road-race car.

systems.name: Steering
systems.summary: Gen 6 Camaro uses a ZF rack-mounted electric power steering (variable-ratio rack-and-pinion) bolted to the front cradle, a collapsible tilt/telescope column and a two-piece intermediate shaft. Race builds keep the ZF EPS rack (no bolt-in race rack exists), add a quick-release race wheel, and correct bump steer with adjustable outer tie rod ends.
systems.overview:
The steering gear is a ZF rack with the assist motor and controller mounted on the rack (GM: 'ZF rack-mounted electric, power-assisted and variable ratio rack-and-pinion'), turning circle 38.4 ft on the ZL1. The rack bolts to the front cradle; inner tie rods thread onto the rack bar and outer tie rod ends taper into the knuckle steering arms (the model places the rack ahead of the axle line - verify on your car). The column is collapsible with an electric column lock and steering angle sensor; a two-piece intermediate shaft passes the dash panel and runs beside the driver-side exhaust to the pinion.

Keeping EPS in a race car: the controller needs a heavy 12 V feed and ground, an ignition/wake signal and GM CAN messages (vehicle speed etc.). With a standalone engine ECU/PDM, plan a strategy (retain the needed GM modules on a private CAN, or use a gateway/emulator) during electrical design. The ZL1 1LE shipped with 'power steering deflectors' for track use, indicating EPS heat is a concern - duct cool air to it and log supply voltage.

Race cockpit: quick-release wheel (NRG, Works Bell, OMP, Sparco), a Gen 6-specific hub adapter, and button/horn wiring through a contact QR or coiled cord. Removing the airbag wheel requires properly disabling SRS. Rules (NASA CCR / SCCA GCR) commonly allow aftermarket wheels and quick releases; check class rules regarding retaining collapsible columns and airbags.

Common issues: torn rack boots from header heat, inner tie rod wear, U-joint pinch bolts not seated in spline grooves, lash in cheap quick releases, bump steer after lowering.
buildNotes: Bolt rack to front cradle on the bench; center the rack.
Install tie rods, set approximate toe (count threads).
Install column on IP beam or cage dash bar; install intermediate shafts with rack and wheel centered.
Wire EPS (phase 8): heavy feed, ground, wake, CAN.
Fit hub adapter, quick release, race wheel and button wiring (phase 9).
Set alignment toe and measure/correct bump steer with adjustable TREs (phase 11); recalibrate SAS if factory ABS/ESC retained.

subsystems.name: Steering Column & Intermediate Shafts
subsystems.description: Collapsible tilt/telescope steering column mounted to the instrument-panel beam (or a cage dash bar in a race car), plus a two-piece intermediate shaft with U-joints that passes through the dash panel and down beside the engine to the rack pinion.

subsystems.name: Steering Rack (ZF Rack-Mounted Electric Power Steering)
subsystems.description: Factory ZF variable-ratio rack-and-pinion with the electric assist motor and controller mounted on the rack (not the column), bolted to the front cradle. For a road-race car the factory EPS rack is normally retained because no bolt-in manual or hydraulic race rack exists for the Alpha cradle; the challenge is powering and networking it outside the factory electrical system.

subsystems.name: Tie Rods
subsystems.description: Inner tie rods (ball joint threaded onto the rack bar), outer tie rod ends (tapered stud into the knuckle steering arm) and the jam nuts that lock toe.

subsystems.name: Steering Wheel & Quick Release
subsystems.description: Race steering wheel, quick-release coupling and the hub adapter (boss) that fits the Gen 6 column spline, plus button/horn wiring through the quick release.

subsystems.name: Bump Steer Correction
subsystems.description: Bump steer is toe change with suspension travel caused by the tie rod not following the arc of the lower links/strut. Lowering a Gen 6 Camaro or changing radius rods/LCAs changes it; it is corrected by moving the outer tie rod pivot height with an adjustable tie rod end and spacers, measured with a bump-steer gauge.

systems.name: Brakes
systems.summary: The Gen 6 ZL1 / ZL1 1LE arrives with Brembo 6-piston front (390x36 mm two-piece rotors) and 4-piston rear (365x28 mm) calipers, a vacuum booster with tandem master cylinder, a four-channel ABS/StabiliTrak modulator and an electronic cable-puller park brake. A bare-shell race build normally removes the booster and factory ABS electronics in favor of a floor-mount dual-master pedal box with a cockpit-adjustable balance bar, optionally a Bosch Motorsport ABS kit, stainless -3 plumbing, race pads/fluid and full front brake ducting – or upgrades to AP Racing / Wilwood race calipers.
systems.overview:
How it works: pedal force is multiplied by the pedal ratio, split by the balance bar between a front and a rear master cylinder, converted to hydraulic pressure, optionally modulated by ABS, and delivered through hard lines and flex hoses to opposed-piston calipers that clamp vented iron rotors. On the factory car the vacuum booster adds force and the EBCM provides electronic brake-force distribution (there is no mechanical proportioning valve).

Key decisions for a road-race Camaro: (1) keep or delete ABS – the factory EBCM/BPMV needs the factory CAN environment (ECM torque, steering angle, yaw), so with a stand-alone race ECU it is either replaced by a Bosch Motorsport M5/M7 kit or deleted; (2) caliper package – the factory ZL1 6-pots are strong but their dust boots cook on a full race car and pad volume is small (~15.8 mm), so Essex/AP Radi-CAL kits (25 mm pads, D62 heavy-duty option, 390 mm for high power) or Wilwood SX6R are common; (3) wheel size – 390 mm ZL1 rotors force 19 in wheels, while the Essex 372 mm kit fits behind 18 in ATS-V-size wheels, which opens up cheaper 18 in slicks; (4) cooling – a heavy car with 600+ hp must have rotor-eye ducting.

Rules: NASA and SCCA production-based classes generally allow brake upgrades and ABS changes within class-specific limits (check your class: some spec/production classes require OEM calipers or restrict ABS); all series require a functioning dual-circuit system, brake lights, and secure lines inside the cockpit (no fittings where the driver can be sprayed – route through bulkheads). Trans Am TA2-style rules mandate specific spec components. Always confirm with the current rulebook before buying.

Common failure points: boiled fluid (long pedal) from insufficient ducting or old fluid; cracked rotors; caliper boots/seals cooked; pad knock-back from worn hub bearings; flex hose chafe; loose bleeders or reused crush washers; torque-to-yield hat/caliper bolts reused; EPB shoes dragging; ABS sensor wiring melted near the caliper.
buildNotes: Phase 1: fabricate pedal-box floor plate and drill firewall bulkhead holes for lines before paint.
Phase 2: mount pedal box and masters, remote reservoirs, ABS unit (if used), and bend/clamp all hard lines (front via firewall bulkheads, rear down the floor) while the shell is empty.
Phase 3–4: after suspension: install duct backing plates (or shields), hub bearings, rotors, calipers (bleeders up!), flex hoses with new crush washers, park brake (if kept).
Pressure-test the hydraulic system before installing interior panels: hold pedal hard 60 s, no drop, no weeps.
Phase 8: wire brake light/pressure sensors, ABS power/CAN, wheel speed sensors to PDM/logger.
Phase 10: brake duct inlets in fascia/splitter and hose routing; check steering lock/bump clearance.
Phase 11: fill with DOT 4 racing fluid, bleed RR-LR-RF-LF (inner then outer), set balance bar baseline, bed pads, verify bias with pressure sensors on track.

schematics.title: Race brake hydraulic circuit (dual masters, balance bar, Bosch ABS optional)
schematics.description: Driver input through a floor-mount pedal and balance bar to separate front and rear master cylinders, each with its own reservoir. Pressure transducers tee off each circuit. The Bosch Motorsport ABS hydraulic unit sits between the masters and the corners (or is replaced by a front tee and a rear tee for an ABS-delete car). Front circuit: two hard lines through firewall bulkheads to the LF/RF hose brackets, flex hoses to 6-piston calipers. Rear circuit: one line under/inside the floor to a tee on the rear subframe, then to LR/RR flex hoses and 4-piston calipers.

schematics.title: Factory brake hydraulic circuit (booster, tandem MC, 4-channel ABS/ESC)
schematics.description: GM Gen 6 ZL1 layout: pedal pushrod into vacuum booster (manifold vacuum, auxiliary pump on some engines), tandem master cylinder with shared reservoir (also feeding the clutch master), two pipes to the BPMV with the EBCM bolted on, four outlet pipes – one per wheel – to the flex hoses and Brembo calipers. EBD is done electronically by the EBCM.

schematics.title: Front brake cooling airflow
schematics.description: Ram air enters fascia/splitter inlets, travels through 3 in duct hose to the backing plate that replaces the dust shield, enters the rotor eye at the hat, is pumped outward by the directional vanes and exits at the rotor OD, carrying heat away from the ring and (indirectly) the pads and caliper.

schematics.title: Factory electronic park brake (J77 cable puller, drum-in-hat)
schematics.description: Console switch → EPB module (motor + gear) → intermediate cable/equalizer → left and right rear cables → shoe levers inside each rear rotor hat (drum). Service requires scan-tool release mode.

subsystems.name: Pedal Box & Brake Bias
subsystems.description: Driver input end of the brake system. Factory: GM hanging pedal bracket pushing a vacuum booster. Race: floor-mount pedal box with a threaded balance bar splitting pedal force between separate front and rear master cylinders, adjustable from the cockpit by a remote cable.

subsystems.name: ABS / Stability Control
subsystems.description: Factory four-channel ABS with StabiliTrak/ESC and Performance Traction Management: an Electronic Brake Control Module (EBCM) mounted to the Brake Pressure Modulator Valve (BPMV). Race options: keep the factory unit (requires factory CAN/ECM/steering-angle environment), install a stand-alone Bosch Motorsport ABS kit, or delete ABS entirely with a dual-master bias bar.

subsystems.name: Booster, Master Cylinders & Reservoirs
subsystems.description: Converts pedal force into hydraulic pressure. Factory: vacuum booster + tandem (dual-circuit) master cylinder on the driver-side firewall feeding the ABS/ESC modulator. Race: no booster; two independent master cylinders (front and rear) on the balance bar, each with its own remote reservoir.

subsystems.name: Brake Lines, Hoses & Fittings
subsystems.description: Rigid lines from the master cylinder(s) through the ABS (if fitted) to each corner, then flexible hoses across the suspension to the calipers. Factory: 3/16 in (4.76 mm) coated steel tube with metric ISO bubble flares, rubber flex hoses with banjo fittings. Race: same-size tube (steel or Cunifer) with -3 AN 37° ends or retained metric ends plus PTFE stainless-braided -3 hoses.

subsystems.name: Brake Cooling
subsystems.description: Ducts that take high-pressure air from the front fascia/splitter and feed it to the eye (center) of each front rotor so the vanes pump it out through the ring. A heavy (~3,700 lb) car with 600+ hp needs ducting to keep pads in their window and fluid below boiling. Rear ducting is optional.

subsystems.name: Front Calipers
subsystems.description: Fixed, opposed-piston calipers bolted directly to the front knuckle (no bracket on the factory Brembo installs). ZL1/ZL1 1LE: Brembo 6-piston monobloc (2x38, 2x34, 2x30 mm). Race: AP Racing Radi-CAL (Essex kits) or Wilwood SX6R on radial-mount brackets. Calipers sit behind the axle centerline (trailing) on the Gen 6.

subsystems.name: Front Pads
subsystems.description: Friction material. The single biggest tuning item for a race car: pick a race compound with a temperature window that matches the car (a 3,700+ lb Camaro on slicks needs a high-temp endurance pad). Factory ZL1 Brembo pads are ~15.8 mm thick; AP CP9668 pads are 25 mm.

subsystems.name: Front Rotors
subsystems.description: ZL1 / ZL1 1LE front: 390 x 36 mm two-piece rotors (cast-iron friction ring bolted to a separate hat). GM notes the 1LE two-piece fronts cannot be machined. Race: fully floating two-piece discs (AP J-hook, DBA 5000 rings, Girodisc) on aluminum bells with drive bobbins.

subsystems.name: Parking Brake
subsystems.description: Gen 6 Camaro uses an electronic parking brake (EPB). Cars with single-piston rear calipers (RPO J71) have a motor on each caliper; cars with the fixed Brembo rears such as ZL1 (RPO J77) use an electric cable-puller module pulling cables to drum-in-hat shoes inside the rear rotors. Race: keep (some rules/transport needs), convert to a hydraulic handbrake, or delete.

subsystems.name: Rear Calipers
subsystems.description: ZL1 / ZL1 1LE (J6G): Brembo 4-piston fixed rear calipers (2x32, 2x28 mm) bolted directly to the rear knuckle, 365 x 28 mm one-piece rotors. Base/SS non-1LE (JL9/J55): single-piston floating caliper on a bracket. Race: AP Radi-CAL 4-piston (Essex rear kit) retaining the OEM drum-in-hat park brake.

subsystems.name: Rear Pads
subsystems.description: Rear pad compound is often one step less aggressive than the front to keep the rear stable on corner entry; matching compounds front/rear is the default starting point.

subsystems.name: Rear Rotors
subsystems.description: ZL1 / ZL1 1LE rear: 365 x 28 mm vented one-piece rotor whose hat doubles as the parking-brake drum (drum-in-hat). Race: two-piece floating disc with a drum-in-hat compatible bell (Essex/AP 365x30) or a park-brake delete.

subsystems.name: Brake Fluid, Bleeding & Bedding
subsystems.description: Fluid choice, fill, bleed sequence, bedding procedure and between-session service. Glycol DOT 4 racing fluid with a high dry boiling point is the standard for road racing; it absorbs moisture, so it is replaced often.

systems.name: Wheels, Tires & Hubs
systems.summary: Gen 6 Camaro corners use bolt-on sealed hub bearings (front non-driven, rear splined with an axle nut), 5x120 mm M14x1.5 studs, and 60° conical lug nuts at 190 N·m (140 ft-lb). The ZL1 1LE runs forged 19x11 ET≈11 / 19x12 ET≈41 wheels on Goodyear Eagle F1 SuperCar 3R 305/30R19 and 325/30R19; race builds use lightweight forged 18–19 in wheels on R-compounds or slicks, with extended studs, open-end nuts and TPMS deleted or replaced by motorsport TPMS.
systems.overview:
Stack-up (outboard): knuckle → hub bearing (bolted from inboard) → wheel studs pressed in the hub flange → rotor hat (or one-piece rotor) → optional hub-centric spacer → wheel (hub-centric on 66.9 mm pilot) → lug nuts. Rear adds the halfshaft CV stub through the splined hub, clamped by the axle nut.

Race considerations: wheel diameter is dictated by the brake package (factory 390 mm rotors need 19 in; Essex/AP 372 mm kits clear 18 in ATS-V-size wheels). Offsets near OE (front ET≈11 on 11 in, rear ET≈41 on 12 in) keep scrub radius and fender clearance sane; ZL1 1LE owners commonly run ≈ -3.2° front camber. Many rulebooks set a maximum wheel width/tire size per class and require full thread engagement of lug nuts (≥ 1x stud diameter) – fit extended studs whenever spacers or thick race-wheel pads are used.

Hub bearings are consumables on a slick-shod 3,700 lb car: check play every event and replace on a schedule; worn bearings cause pad knock-back and long pedal. Re-torque lug nuts after the first session on freshly mounted wheels and never use an impact gun for final torque.
buildNotes: Phase 4 (after suspension): install front/rear hub bearings with new bolts (front 100 N·m first pass + GM final angle; rear 130 N·m), wheel speed sensors, then brakes.
Press extended studs (if used) with hubs on the bench before installation.
Phase 6: insert halfshafts and torque new rear axle nuts (270 N·m) with the car on the ground or rotor locked.
Template-check race wheels against the chosen calipers before ordering; specify offset to match OE track unless suspension is re-engineered.
Mount/balance tires; install metal valve stems or motorsport TPMS; record sensor IDs.
Phase 11: torque lug nuts 190 N·m (140 ft-lb) in star pattern, re-check after first shakedown session; set cold pressures from hot targets.

subsystems.name: Front Hubs & Bearings
subsystems.description: Non-driven front corners use a sealed, bolt-on hub bearing unit (Gen 3 style) with pressed wheel studs and an integral magnetic ABS encoder, bolted to the front knuckle from the inboard side.

subsystems.name: Rear Hubs & Bearings
subsystems.description: Driven rear corners: bolt-in hub bearing unit with splined bore; the halfshaft outer CV stub passes through and is retained by an axle (drive-shaft) nut.

subsystems.name: TPMS
subsystems.description: Factory direct TPMS: a battery-powered pressure sensor on each valve stem transmits to the body control module/receiver. With the factory body electronics removed it serves no purpose; race cars either delete it or fit a motorsport TPMS that reports to the dash/logger.

subsystems.name: Wheel Spacers (if used)
subsystems.description: Hub-centric slip-on spacers used to fine-tune track width or clear calipers. Always pair with extended studs so lug nuts engage at least the stud diameter (full nut preferred). Bolt-on adapters (spacer with its own studs) add a joint and are banned or discouraged in some classes.

subsystems.name: Wheel Studs & Lug Nuts
subsystems.description: 5 x 120 mm bolt pattern, M14 x 1.5 studs pressed into the hub flanges, 60° conical-seat lug nuts torqued to 190 N·m (140 ft-lb). Race builds fit longer studs for thick race wheels/spacers and open-ended race nuts.

subsystems.name: Wheels
subsystems.description: Factory ZL1 1LE: forged aluminum 19x11 front / 19x12 rear (OE offsets ≈ ET11 / ET41). ZL1: 20x10 / 20x11 forged. Race: lightweight forged 18 or 19 in wheels sized for slicks; the brake package decides the minimum diameter (390 mm ZL1 rotors/6-pots need 19 in; Essex 372 mm kits fit 18 in ATS-V-size wheels).

subsystems.name: Tires
subsystems.description: Factory ZL1 1LE: Goodyear Eagle F1 SuperCar 3R 305/30R19 front, 325/30R19 rear (good for ~1.10 g). ZL1: Eagle F1 SuperCar 3 285/30ZR20 / 305/30ZR20. Race: DOT R-compound or slicks on 18–19 in wheels; pressures set by hot targets measured immediately after the session.

systems.name: Engine
systems.summary: A GM Gen V small-block 6.2 L (LT4 supercharged from the ZL1 as the baseline, LT1 noted) built for road racing. The long block uses an aluminum 4.065 x 3.622 in block, forged crank, reverse-cooled DI heads, VVT cam and an Eaton R1740 supercharger-manifold. Race builds keep the architecture but add ARP studs, forged/coated internals, AFM delete with a locked or limited phaser, upgraded valve springs, better oil control (baffled wet sump or dry sump) and fuel system upgrades (XDI or port injection).
systems.overview:
Architecture. The Gen V LT is a 90° pushrod V8 with 4.400 in bore spacing, 9.240 in deck and the 1-8-7-2-6-5-4-3 firing order. Odd cylinders 1-3-5-7 are on the left (driver) bank from front to rear and the left bank sits forward of the right. Unlike the LS it has direct injection, with the injector in the chamber between the valves and a single high-pressure pump driven by a 4-lobe lobe at the back of the cam. It also has a vane-type VVT phaser with a center-bolt spool valve worked by a solenoid on the front cover, a variable-displacement crank-driven oil pump, and reverse-flow cooling.

LT4 vs LT1. The ZL1 LT4 runs 10.0:1 compression with forged pistons, rotocast A356 heads (65.47 cc), titanium intake valves and a 1.7 L Eaton R1740 TVS blower at about 9.2-9.7 psi. It has a larger HP fuel pump and 141 lb/hr DI injectors, and the wet sump holds 10 qt. The LT1 (SS/1LE) runs 11.5:1 with cast pistons, 59 cc 319-T7 heads, steel valves and a composite NA manifold. The bottom end hardware and most torque specs are shared.

Road-race priorities. (1) Oil control under sustained lateral g: a baffled ZL1 pan is adequate for many club racers, but hard-tire or slick cars should move to a dry sump (Fluidworks 5-511/5-611 integral pan/pump kits, or Katech dry-sump pump plus an engine-support tank). (2) Heat: watch intercooler circuit capacity, oil temperature and plug heat range. (3) Valvetrain stability: AFM delete with LS7-style lifters, dual springs, trunnion upgrade, a locked or limited phaser and 3/8 in pushrods. (4) Fuel: the stock LT4 DI system runs out around stock power at high rpm, so for more power use XDI injectors with a pump upgrade, or add port injection. (5) Fasteners: GM uses torque-to-yield bolts almost everywhere (heads, mains, rods, balancer, cam bolt, flywheel), so budget new bolts or ARP studs.

Rules. NASA ST/TT and SCCA classes generally allow engine swaps and internal changes with power-to-weight or dyno-sheet limits. Check your class rules for crankcase venting (sealed catch can required), oil drain plug safety wire, SFI-rated balancer/flywheel requirements and fuel type (E85/race gas affects DI vs PI choice).

Common failure points. Watch for AFM lifter collapse, rocker trunnion bearings, and the variable-vane oil pump (do not reuse one after removal). Other weak spots are supercharger belt slip and tensioner wear, DI pump/follower wear (watch the commanded vs actual rail pressure gap), head-bolt threads not chased before reassembly, and oil starvation in long sweepers on a wet sump.
buildNotes: Decide the target first (LT4 boosted vs LT1 NA, power level, wet vs dry sump, DI vs PI). It dictates pistons, cam, fuel lobe, pan and ECU.
Machine the block: hot-tank, remove all plugs, chase all threads (factory head-bolt thread compound!), align hone on ARP main studs if used, and bore/hone with a deck plate.
Assemble the short block on the stand: cam bearings, cam and retainer plate, main bearings, crank, main caps (inner, outer, side fastener order), then pistons and rods with measured clearances.

Install the rear cover/seal, then the timing set with the phaser (and limiter, if used). Degree the cam, then fit the oil pump with a new inlet O-ring, the pickup, the front cover/seal and the oil pan.

Fit the heads on new MLS gaskets with GM TTY bolts (59 ft-lb +90° +60°) or ARP studs (40/80/115 ft-lb). Then install the lifters/trays, pushrods and rockers (22 ft-lb with each lifter on the base circle).

Install the DI system: HPFP follower, then the pump (with the lobe on base circle), then new injector seals, rails and HP line (21 ft-lb). Next fit the valve covers, plugs (15 ft-lb), coils and sensors.

Install the water pump and the balancer: seat it with the old bolt or an installer, then fit a new TTY bolt (89 ft-lb, back off one turn, 59 ft-lb, then +125° or +200°). Add the supercharger with all 8 port gaskets, then the belts.
Pre-lube the oil system with a pressure primer, set the base timing and VVT strategy in the calibration, and pressure/vacuum test the intercooler and cooling circuits.
Break in on the dyno, then change the oil and filter and cut the filter open. Do a leak-down baseline and record it for comparison between events.

schematics.title: Timing drive & valvetrain (with VVT and DI pump drive)
schematics.description: Crank-to-valve motion path, VVT control loop and the cam-driven DI pump. Torque values in labels are the key fasteners in each joint.

schematics.title: Crankcase ventilation (PCV) - LT4 factory vs road-race
schematics.description: Fresh air enters the crankcase through the valve-cover fresh-air port from the clean side of the inlet; blow-by is drawn through the oil separator/PCV orifice into the supercharger (LT4) under vacuum. Under boost the fresh-air side can reverse. Race setup adds catch/breather cans; a dry-sump car vents through the oil tank.

schematics.title: Direct-injection high-pressure fuel circuit (and optional PI)
schematics.description: Low-pressure supply from the tank module feeds the cam-driven HP pump, which delivers up to ~2,900+ psi to both DI rails. ECM closes the loop with the rail pressure sensor and the pump flow-control valve. Optional port-injection rails take low-pressure fuel directly.

schematics.title: On-engine lubrication path (wet sump)
schematics.description: Oil path inside the engine for the factory wet sump. With a dry sump the pan/pump are replaced (engine-support owns the external pump, tank and lines) but the galleries downstream of the filter are the same.

schematics.title: Accessory and supercharger belt drives
schematics.description: Two belt planes off the balancer: the inner 6-rib accessory belt and the outer 8-rib supercharger belt. Pulley positions are approximate - verify against your bracket set.

systems.name: Engine Support (oil, cooling, fuel, intake, exhaust)
systems.summary: Everything that keeps the race LT engine alive but is not the long block: dry-sump lubrication, engine coolant circuit, the LT4 supercharger low-temp intercooler loop, FT3 fuel cell and surge-tank fuel delivery, induction, exhaust, breathers, and the front cooler stack. The ZL1 baseline is a WET-sump LT4 with a returnless PWM fuel system and an 11-heat-exchanger cooling package; the race build converts to a dry sump, a trunk-mounted FT3 cell with a surge tank and a constant ~72 psi low-side supply, long-tube headers and a fully ducted cooling stack.
systems.overview:
Factory baseline. Contrary to a common assumption, the 6th-gen Camaro ZL1 LT4 is wet-sump (~10 qt, GM TechLink lists Camaro LT1/LT4 at 9.5 L / 10.0 qt of 0W-40); only the C7 Corvette Z51/Z06 LT engines got GM's factory dry sump. The ZL1 feeds its direct-injection high-pressure pump from a returnless, PWM-controlled in-tank pump (≈58 psi cruise / ≈72 psi WOT). Cooling is a large radiator plus a separate low-temperature loop (front heat exchanger, electric pump) for the supercharger's two intercooler bricks, and the track package adds engine oil, transmission and differential coolers.

Lubrication. Sustained road-race g-loads on slicks starve a wet sump, so the race build uses a billet dry-sump pan with 4-5 scavenge stages (one per crank-bay pair plus timing case), a belt-driven external pump with built-in pressure regulation, a de-aerating remote tank in the right front of the engine bay, a remote filter, a thermostatically controlled oil cooler in the right front corner, and -16/-12 AN plumbing. If the engine must stay wet-sump, run a trap-door baffle and an Accusump.

Cooling. Keep the engine circuit (radiator + pressurized surge/degas tank + 160-180 °F thermostat) and the LT4 intercooler loop completely separate. The IC heat exchanger sits first in the airflow. Duct every core so no air bypasses, vent the exit air through the hood, and use water + surfactant instead of glycol where the track bans antifreeze. Upgrading the IC heat exchanger and reservoir volume is the most effective cure for ZL1 heat soak.

Fuel. The factory saddle tank is removed and an FIA FT3 cell (e.g., Fuel Safe ED122B 22 gal / 19.3 usable) sits in a steel or aluminum can in the trunk behind the axle, behind a sealed bulkhead (NASA CCR 15.4.1.1; SCCA metal bulkhead). From 2026 NASA requires the cell to be entirely rearward of the seat rear mounts. FT3 certification expires 5 years after manufacture. A lift pump keeps a surge tank full; twin feed pumps in the surge tank supply a bypass regulator at the tank (short-loop return) so only one -8 line runs forward, under the passenger floor, to the engine-driven DI pump. Hold low-side pressure at ≈72 psi (not below 68 psi with a Lingenfelter big-bore DI pump).

Exhaust. Stainless long-tubes (1-7/8 in common, 2 in for big power) replace the ZL1 tri-Y manifolds; check dry-sump pump and steering-shaft clearance. Use V-band collectors, wideband O2 per bank, a 3 in X-pipe in the tunnel, flex joints, and race mufflers behind the axle (or side exits if rules/sound allow). Heat-shield the tunnel, floor and the trunk floor under the fuel cell.

Common failure points: dry-sump belt failure (carry spares, guard it), oil blowing out the tank breather (overfilled tank/undersized vent), fuel pressure drop in long corners (lift pump/pickup), expired or foam-degraded cells, cracked header flanges/loose header bolts, air trapped in the IC loop, and undersized or poorly ducted radiators.
buildNotes: Phase 1: weld fuel-cell cradle, strap anchors, rear bulkhead, oil-tank and cooler-stack brackets before paint; remove factory tank, EVAP and fuel lines.
Phase 2: install the fuel cell, surge tank, pumps, filters, regulator and run the single -8 feed line and vent lines while the chassis is bare.
Phase 5 (engine on stand): fit dry-sump pan, pump bracket, mandrel, pulleys, belt and pump fittings; verify pickup clearances; set up header clearance mock-up.
Phase 6: install engine/trans; confirm pan-to-ground and header clearances at race ride height.

Phase 7: install headers and exhaust from the front back; then oil tank, filter, thermostat, cooler and all -AN oil lines; then cooler stack, radiator, IC heat exchanger, pump and reservoir, all coolant hoses; then intake and breathers.
Phase 8: wire pumps and fans through the PDM with kill-switch and stall shutoff; add oil/fuel/coolant pressure and temperature sensors.

Phase 11: fill fuel and leak-check at pressure; prime oil system (ignition/fuel disabled) until pressure registers; vacuum-fill engine coolant and IC loop; first start, check leaks, bleed, re-torque header/clamps after heat cycle; set dry-sump tank level hot at idle.

schematics.title: Dry-sump oil circuit
schematics.description: Complete dry-sump path: crankcase is scavenged by 4 pump stages into the tank, de-aerated oil feeds the pressure stage, then filter → thermostat (→ cooler) → engine gallery. Tank vents to the catch can. Optional Accusump on the pressure side.

schematics.title: Engine coolant circuit (high-temp)
schematics.description: Water pump → block/heads → water outlet → upper hose → radiator → lower hose → thermostat housing → pump. Degas lines from the radiator and the engine high point feed the pressurized surge tank, whose make-up line returns solid coolant to the pump inlet. Heater core deleted with a bypass loop.

schematics.title: LT4 supercharger intercooler loop (low-temp)
schematics.description: Electric pump → supercharger intercooler bricks → reservoir (degas) → front heat exchanger → pump. Completely separate from the engine coolant circuit.

schematics.title: Fuel system (cell → surge → feed → DI pump)
schematics.description: Cell pickup → 100 µm pre-filter → lift pump → surge tank → twin feed pumps → 10 µm filter → bypass regulator (~72 psi) with short-loop return to the surge tank → single -8 feed line → bulkheads → engine dry-break → DI high-pressure pump (engine). Surge overflow returns to the cell; cell vents through a rollover valve.

schematics.title: Exhaust flow
schematics.description: Each bank: 4 primaries → collector → V-band → catted/test connection pipe (wideband O2) → X-pipe → flex → mid pipe → muffler → tip. Side-exit option branches after the X-pipe.

schematics.title: Air intake path & crankcase ventilation
schematics.description: Fascia snorkel → sealed air box → filter → MAF/IAT → intake tube → couplers → throttle body → LT4 supercharger. Crankcase/tank vapors go to the catch can; can vents to filter or the fresh-air port.

routes.name: Main feed: regulator → engine DI pump (-8)

subsystems.name: Fuel Cell
subsystems.description: FIA FT3 fuel cell (bladder + foam + can) mounted in the trunk behind the rear axle with fill plate, rollover vent valve, vent line, filler/check valve, level sender, straps, cradle and the cockpit bulkhead required by NASA CCR 15.4 / SCCA GCR.

subsystems.name: Fuel Delivery (low-pressure supply to the DI pump)
subsystems.description: Cell → pre-filter → lift pump → surge tank → twin feed pumps → 10-micron filter → bypass regulator (short-loop return at the tank, ~72 psi) → single -8 feed line under the passenger-side floor → engine-bay dry break → DI high-pressure pump inlet (engine system).

subsystems.name: Lubrication (dry-sump oiling)
subsystems.description: Converts the ZL1 LT4 (factory wet sump, ~10 qt) to a multi-stage dry-sump system: billet pan, belt-driven external pump, remote de-aerating tank, remote filter, thermostatically controlled oil cooler and -12/-16 AN plumbing.

Includes hangers, valve deletes, coatings and heat shields.

subsystems.name: LT4 Supercharger Intercooler Low-Temp Loop

systems.name: Drivetrain
systems.summary: Front-mid LT V8 drives through a flywheel and clutch into a TREMEC TR-6060 six-speed (ZL1 1LE RPO MH3, 650 lb-ft rated), a two-piece propeller shaft and a cradle-mounted 226 mm differential with GM eLSD (3.73:1) feeding independent rear halfshafts. Race builds typically fit a twin/multi-disc clutch with an adjustable HRB in an SFI bellhousing, a stronger H-pattern or sequential gearbox, a one-piece carbon driveshaft with safety loops, a mechanical race LSD with solid diff mounts, upgraded halfshafts, and ducted trans/diff oil coolers.
systems.overview:
Layout. On the Gen 6 (Alpha platform) Camaro the engine sits behind the front axle with the bellhousing face at about x=0.38 m. The TREMEC 6060 (TR-6060) is a fully synchronized aluminum-case six-speed with triple-cone 1st/2nd and double-cone 3rd-6th/reverse synchronizers, tapered-roller main and countershaft bearings, solenoid 2-3 skip-shift and reverse inhibit, and a remote shifter linked by an external shift rod. GM rates it at 650 lb-ft (881 N·m). The ZL1 1LE close-ratio MH3 box runs 2.29/1.61/1.21/1.00/0.82/0.68 (R 3.11) with a 3.73 final drive; 2016+ SS uses 2.66/1.78/1.30/1.00/0.74/0.50. The factory propeller shaft is two-piece with rubber flex couplers at both ends and a center support bearing. The 226 mm differential bolts into the rear cradle on two front bushings and one rear bushing (rear bolt is torque-angle-yield, 162 ft-lb + 60°), with plug-in halfshafts retained by circlips.

Key road-race decisions. (1) Clutch: factory twin-disc copes with 650 lb-ft on the street but a race car benefits from a lower-inertia twin/multi-disc pack and an adjustable hydraulic release bearing (Tilton 60-6241 / 60-6111 list TR6060 applications) with a remote bleeder. (2) Containment: fit an SFI 6.x steel bellhousing (or SFI blanket where permitted) and dial-indicate runout. (3) Gearbox: TR-6060 is durable when cooled and shifted cleanly; for endurance or a high-output custom engine consider a TREMEC Magnum XL (700 lb-ft) or a sequential dog box (Holinger RD6-S 880 N·m endurance rating, Xtrac as on the Camaro GT4.R) with paddle shift. (4) Driveshaft: replace the two-piece shaft and flex discs with a one-piece carbon or aluminum shaft (DSS GMCA19-C, QA1 JJ-22208) and add safety loops. (5) Differential: the eLSD is excellent but depends on GM network control; with a standalone race ECU most builders convert to a mechanical plate LSD and solid-mount the diff (BMR BK058/BK059/BK060). (6) Cooling: GM fits trans and diff coolers to the ZL1 1LE and warns of high axle temps on the first track day; race cars need ducted coolers with thermostats and temp logging.

Rules. Most sanctioning bodies (NASA, SCCA, Trans Am, etc.) have drivetrain safety requirements that vary by class: SFI-rated bellhousing or flywheel shield, driveshaft safety loop(s), catch cans for gearbox/axle breathers, lockwired drain plugs and sealed tunnel/shifter openings. Always check your class rulebook and tech inspector.

Fluids and intervals (GM). Manual transmission fluid change every 15 h of track use. Rear axle fluid needs 1,500 mi (2,400 km) break-in before track use; drain and refill after the first event then every 24 h of racing. ZL1 coupe with eLSD: 1.5 L axle fluid + 160 mL eLSD actuation fluid; LT1 non-eLSD axle 1.1 L. Clutch shares DOT 4 with the brakes.

Common failure points. Torn flex couplers and center bearing isolators, CV boot tears from exhaust heat, diff bushing deflection/wheel hop, overheated diff/gearbox oil, HRB seal failure from over-stroking, clutch contamination from input/rear-main seals, and loose AN fittings inside the bellhousing.
buildNotes: Phase 3: with the rear cradle on the car (suspension team), install diff mount bushings/lockouts, raise the differential into the cradle and torque front bolts then the rear TAY bolt (new bolt).
Phase 4: install halfshafts (seal protector, circlip pull-test) and torque axle nuts to GM SI with wheels loaded.
Phase 5: engine on stand - pilot bearing, dial-indicate bellhousing runout (offset dowels if needed), flywheel (3-pass torque), clutch pack with alignment tool, measure finger height.

Phase 6: set HRB height and plumb its internal hose/bleeder; mate gearbox (pre-filled) to engine; install crossmember/mount; fit driveshaft and safety loops; connect shift rod/shifter; set driveline angles.
Phase 6: route -3 AN clutch line to the bulkhead; bleed via remote bleeder; set pedal over-travel stop.
Phase 7: plumb trans and diff cooler circuits (pump below oil level, filter, thermostat, ducted cooler), vents to catch cans.
Phase 8: wire sensors (trans temp, diff temp, gear position, clutch position, VSS, reverse lockout), pump control in PDM, eLSD (if retained) or delete strategy, sequential GCU if fitted.
Phase 11: fill gearbox and axle (plus cooler volume), bleed coolers, check for leaks, break in axle per GM before hard track use, re-torque driveline fasteners after shakedown and paint-mark them.

schematics.title: Power flow: crankshaft to rear wheels
schematics.description: Torque path from the LT crankshaft through flywheel, clutch, gearbox, driveshaft, differential and halfshafts to the rear hubs, plus the reaction paths through the transmission mount/crossmember and the differential mounts into the rear cradle and body.

schematics.title: Clutch hydraulic circuit
schematics.description: Pedal to master cylinder to release bearing. Factory: shared brake/clutch reservoir, OEM pipe and concentric slave. Race: dedicated reservoir, -3 AN braided line, bellhousing bulkhead, adjustable HRB with remote bleeder and pedal over-travel stop. Pedal sensor feeds ECU for rev-match/launch/flat-shift.

schematics.title: Transmission oil cooling circuit
schematics.description: H-pattern TR-6060: electric pump draws from the low drain-port pickup through a screen, pushes through an in-line filter and thermostat (bypass when cold) to a ducted front cooler, and returns to a high case port. A sequential gearbox (Holinger RD6) replaces the external pump with its internal pump, filter and spray bar but uses the same cooler/thermostat loop.

schematics.title: Differential oil cooling circuit
schematics.description: Electric pump pulls axle oil from a low pickup on the 226 mm diff, through a filter and thermostat to a ducted rear cooler and back to a high return port on the cover. Pump is switched on diff temperature via the PDM.

schematics.title: Sequential paddle-shift control (race option)
schematics.description: Paddles request shifts from the gear control unit (GCU), which fires the pneumatic valve block/actuator on the gearbox selector, reads barrel position, and asks the ECU for ignition cut (upshift) or throttle blip (downshift). Air comes from an on-board compressor/tank. Camaro GT4.R used this concept with an Xtrac sequential.

systems.name: Electrical & Electronics
systems.summary: The Gen 6 Camaro factory electrical system is a GM network architecture (BCM, IPC, GMLAN CAN) with the AGM battery in the trunk, an E92 ECM running the direct-injected LT1/LT4, and underhood/rear fuse-relay blocks. The race build strips the body electronics and replaces them with a purpose-built system: trunk battery with FIA-style master cutoff (mechanical 4-post switch or Cartek solid-state isolator), a programmable PDM instead of fuses/relays, a Chevrolet Performance E92 controller kit or a GDI-capable standalone ECU, a CAN-networked dash/logger, keypad and chassis sensors, and a mil-spec Tefzel/DR-25 harness with Deutsch bulkhead connectors.
systems.overview:
Architecture. Power flows battery (trunk, right side) → master cutoff → main 1/0 cable through the cabin along the passenger sill → firewall power junction → starter, and from the junction (fused) → PDM. The PDM switches and protects every load (ECU, ignition, fuel pumps, fan, intercooler pump, lights, comms) and reports currents over CAN. Grounds return through a dedicated battery-negative cable, two engine-to-chassis straps and a star ground for the electronics. The ECU, PDM, dash/logger, keypad, GPS/IMU, lambda controller, tire-temp sensors and (if used) the race ABS share one or two 1 Mbit/s CAN buses.

Factory vs race. The Gen 6's body modules (BCM, IPC, SDM, radio) are VIN-linked on the GM network and are not needed to run the engine when a Chevrolet Performance LT1/LT4 controller kit is used (the kit supplies a programmed E92, engine harness with fuse box, DBW pedal, O2/MAF, oil and fuel-pressure sensors and the fuel pump power module). Note GM's warning that pre-2022 LT controllers must not be used on 2022+ LT crate engines, and that early (4-pin) and late (3-pin) LT4 fuel-rail pressure sensors need matching kits. The direct-injection LT limits standalone choices to GDI-capable systems (Holley Terminator X Max Gen V LT DI kits 550-1623/550-1624, MoTeC M1 GPR-DI on M122/M142/M182 class ECUs) unless the race engine is converted to port injection (then MoTeC M150, Holley Dominator, Haltech Nexus etc. apply). Keeping OE electric power steering and OE ABS/StabiliTrak requires keeping their network messages alive – decide this with the steering and brakes systems before designing the harness.

Rules. SCCA GCR wording (quoted secondhand) requires a master switch in either battery cable that cuts all electrical circuits except an on-board fire system, accessible from outside – on closed cars in front of the windshield on the cowl/fender (driver side) or below the center of the rear window – marked with the spark/blue-triangle decal. NASA CCR wording (quoted secondhand) allows radio, fire system and life-support devices to remain live. Whether a solid-state isolator is accepted varies by series and inspector – confirm before buying. Rain lights: many series require one; FIA standard 8874-2019 covers homologated rain lights (Lifeline 421-100-011, Cartek CK-LRS-15RM/16CM). Transponder: MyLaps direct-power, ≤ 60 cm above ground with clear view of the track, on a 2.5 A fused switched supply. Always read the current rulebook for your class.

Common failure points. Loose or under-sized main cables (hot restart failures), chafed harness at the firewall/seat/cage crossings, engine-ground straps loosening, connectors not latched, fan and fuel-pump channels tripping on inrush, alternator run-on after the master is switched off (needs field kill / dump resistor), CAN termination errors, and DI injector wiring noise corrupting crank/cam signals.
buildNotes: Phase 1 (bare shell): decide battery, master switch, PDM/ECU and bulkhead locations; weld ground studs and battery box mounts; cut and doubler-plate firewall and rear bulkhead connector holes; install rivnuts for every harness P-clamp along the planned routes; then paint.
Write the electrical load list and channel map (current, PWM, logic) before buying a PDM – fans, fuel pumps, starter and ignition set the channel sizes and the alternator size.
Choose ECU strategy (Chevrolet Performance E92 controller kit vs GDI standalone) and whether OE EPS/ABS are retained before building the harness – it drives CAN design.
Build the cabin electronics panel (PDM, ECU, star ground, fuses) and the dash harness on the bench; build the engine harness on a board measured from the installed engine.
Run the main 1/0 battery cable inside the shell along the passenger sill before seats and interior go in; crimp lugs with a hydraulic crimper and adhesive heat shrink.
Install engine ground straps with the engine (phase 6); install starter, alternator, and their cables before headers if access is tight.

Power-up sequence: continuity test every circuit → check for shorts to ground → first power with ECU/ PDM disconnected → PDM config → ECU power and comms → sensor plausibility → crank with no fuel to verify sync → fuel pressure → first fire.
Verify CAN termination (~60 Ω), ground offsets (< 50 mV ECU-to-battery), master switch kill with engine running, and cranking voltage drop (< 0.5 V positive path) before shakedown.
Install rules items last but test them at the first tech: external kill, decals, rain light, brake lights, transponder.

subsystems.name: Battery & Master Cutoff
subsystems.description: Battery, battery box and hold-down, terminals and lugs, the master electrical cutoff (mechanical 4-post switch or solid-state isolator), internal and external kill switches, alternator field-kill / dump resistor and the main fuse. The Gen 6 Camaro carries its factory battery in the trunk on the right side; this build keeps the battery in the rear (right side, low, ahead of or over the rear axle line) and runs the main cable forward through the cabin.

subsystems.name: Dash & Driver Controls
subsystems.description: Driver display/logger, CAN keypad or switch panel, ignition and start controls, steering-wheel buttons via quick-release connector or wireless system, shift lights, warning lamps and rotary map/traction switches. Replaces the factory IPC, BCM-driven switches and infotainment.

subsystems.name: Grounding
subsystems.description: Grounding scheme: battery negative to chassis (through the isolator), engine block to chassis straps, transmission ground, front and rear chassis ground studs, and a dedicated electronics star ground for the ECU, PDM, logger and sensors. A road-race unibody with seam-welded, painted panels and a welded cage needs deliberate ground paths – paint and seam sealer are insulators.

subsystems.name: Main (Chassis) Harness
subsystems.description: The chassis harness that replaces the factory body harness: firewall bulkhead connector, dash harness, front-to-rear trunk along the tunnel/sill, rear harness to fuel pumps, lights and rear sensors, and the CAN backbone. Built to motorsport standard: M22759/32 (Spec 55) Tefzel wire, Raychem DR-25 jacket, molded boots, Deutsch AS circular connectors for bulkheads, DT/DTM for sensors and loads, cushioned P-clamps and grommets at every panel penetration.

subsystems.name: Sensors (engine & driveline monitoring)
subsystems.description: The electrical system's sensor map. OE engine-control sensors (crank, cam, knock, MAP/TMAP, IAT, ECT, fuel-rail pressure, throttle position, oil pressure) are physically owned by the engine system and are referenced here; this subsystem adds the race monitoring sensors: oil pressure/temperature (logged and alarmed), low-side fuel pressure, coolant pressure, crankcase pressure, EGT per cylinder, transmission and differential temperatures, charge-air temperature and fuel level.

subsystems.name: Data Acquisition
subsystems.description: Logger (usually the dash), GPS/IMU, I/O expander, suspension damper potentiometers, IR tire-temperature arrays, IR brake-rotor temperature, brake pressure, steering angle, wheel speeds and lap beacon receiver. The chassis sensors here are what turn the car into a setup tool.

subsystems.name: Lighting
subsystems.description: Rain light (FIA 8874-2019 homologated LED preferred), brake lights (pressure-switched via PDM), headlights and position/marker lamps for endurance/night events, and their PDM channels and brackets.

subsystems.name: Charging & Starting
subsystems.description: Alternator, starter motor, the long main positive cable from the trunk battery to the engine bay, the front power junction (remote jump post), alternator charge wire and ECM-controlled alternator interface, starter trigger and the clamps/grommets/heat protection along the way.

subsystems.name: Engine Management
subsystems.description: Engine control for the Gen V LT direct-injection engine: factory E92 ECM via a Chevrolet Performance Connect & Cruise / controller kit, or a race standalone with direct-injection capability (Holley Terminator X Max GM Gen V LT DI kit, MoTeC M1 GPR-DI). Includes the engine harness interface, drive-by-wire pedal and throttle, DI injector and high-pressure pump drive, ignition coil sub-harness, wideband lambda, flex-fuel option and tuning access.

subsystems.name: Fans & Pumps Control
subsystems.description: Electrical control and wiring for the high-current motor loads: radiator fan (OE ZL1 brushless PWM fan), fuel pumps (OE ZL1 PWM-controlled pump module or race lift/ surge pumps), LT4 intercooler coolant pump, transmission/diff cooler pumps and fans, cool-suit pump and wiper motor. These are the largest continuous loads and set the alternator and PDM sizing.

subsystems.name: Power Distribution (PDM, fuses, breakers)
subsystems.description: Solid-state Power Distribution Module replacing the factory underhood (X50A) and rear (X51) fuse/relay blocks, plus its power feed, connectors, mounting, a small always-hot fused block for life-support/timing circuits allowed to bypass the master switch where rules permit, and resettable circuit breakers.

subsystems.name: Comms, Video & Timing
subsystems.description: Driver-to-pit radio (radio, car harness, helmet kit, PTT, antenna), in-car video with data overlay, and the timing transponder.

systems.name: Interior
systems.summary: Everything inside the cockpit that is not primary safety structure: stripping the shell, dash and switch panels, pedal-area floor, driver cooling, mirrors, door cards and ballast. The goal is a light, clean, serviceable cockpit with nothing loose and every control reachable while belted.
systems.overview:
A bare-chassis build starts by stripping the Gen 6 shell of all trim, seats, SRS components and asphalt deadener so the cage and seat mounts can be welded to clean metal. The factory IP cross-car beam can be retained to locate the steering column and EPS, with a lightweight race dash panel on top; or the column is hung from the cage dash bar.

The cockpit is laid out around the seated driver: display above the wheel, switch panel and kill/fire controls in the center stack within reach of the belted driver, heel plate and dead pedal in the footwell, cool-suit cooler and fire bottle low on the passenger floor. Door cards close the gutted doors around the door bars.

Ballast must be through-bolted with backing plates (never strapped) and placed low and inboard to help cross-weight.
buildNotes: Strip and de-deadener before cage work.
Decide factory beam vs. cage column support before the dash bar is placed.
Weld all interior mounting tabs to the cage before paint.
Install dash, panels, cooling and mirrors after electrical harness routing.
Add ballast last during corner weighting.

subsystems.name: Pedal Area & Driver Floor

systems.name: Body & Glass
systems.summary: Exterior panels, closures and glazing of the Gen 6 Camaro race car: factory ZL1 panels or lightweight carbon replacements, pinned hood, polycarbonate side/rear windows, quick-release fascias with Dzus fasteners, lighting housings, mirrors and livery.
systems.overview:
The Gen 6 shell is a steel unibody; roof and quarters are welded and stay. Bolt-on panels (hood, fenders, doors, decklid, fascias) can be swapped for composites where class rules allow. Anderson Composites lists Gen 6 carbon hoods (Type-OE AC-HD16CHCAM-OE ~23 lb, Type-CP double-sided ~19 lb, Type-AZ) that require hood pins and a heat shield. AeroCatch flush pins are the common choice; set the pin within ~5° of the latch axis.

Doors are gutted (glass, regulator, intrusion beam removed) so the cage door bars can bow into them, but must still latch. The laminated windshield is retained with retention clips; side and rear glass are replaced by polycarbonate (Margard MR10 is hard-coated but cannot be cold-formed), using oversized holes and nylon washers so the plastic can expand. Fascias and access panels use Dzus EHF5/EHF6 quarter-turn fasteners and rivnuts so the car can be repaired quickly at the track.
buildNotes: Fit panels and set gaps BEFORE paint; mark hinge positions.
Gut doors during cage work (phase 1).
Install hood pins after hood alignment; add cockpit-visible arrows.
Template and fit Lexan after cage/paint.
Install Dzus/rivnuts, then wrap and markings last.

systems.name: Aero
systems.summary: Downforce and drag management for the Gen 6 Camaro: factory ZL1 1LE aero (larger splitter, dive planes, exposed-carbon rear wing, carbon hood vent) as the baseline, or chassis-mounted race splitter, canards, undertray, adjustable wing and diffuser where class rules allow.
systems.overview:
The ZL1 1LE package adds a larger unique splitter, front dive planes and a tall exposed carbon rear wing (RPO T42) to the ZL1; Chevrolet credited it with a 3-second gain around its Milford road course, and one press source quotes ~300 lb of rear downforce at top speed. For racing, the critical difference is load paths: the splitter must be carried by brackets to the crash beam/subframe and adjustable rods, not by the plastic fascia; the wing should load through uprights into mount plates and preferably chassis structure, not the decklid skin.

Balance is tuned with wing angle and Gurney height at the rear against splitter height/extension and canards at the front. Underbody flow is cleaned up with a front undertray (also protecting the oil pan), optional flat mid-floor, rocker-skirt blades and a rear diffuser. Hood extractor and fender louvers reduce front lift and help cooling.

Check every item against the class rules (NASA ST/GTS, SCCA, Trans Am) – splitter overhang, wing span/height and flat bottoms are commonly limited.
buildNotes: Set ride height/rake first.
Mount splitter to chassis brackets, then rods, then fascia edge fasteners.
Fit undertray and side-skirt blades.
Mount wing plates/chassis struts before decklid paint; install uprights, element, endplates, Gurney.
Baseline AoA mid-range; balance during shakedown.

subsystems.name: Rear Diffuser

subsystems.name: Rear Wing

subsystems.name: Side Skirts

subsystems.name: Undertray

components.name: Sound deadener, insulation and undercoat removal
components.description: Removal of factory asphaltic deadener pads, spray-on sound damping, foam baffles and underbody coating in the cockpit, trunk and areas to be welded. Saves weight (typically tens of pounds on a modern coupe) and exposes seams for stitch welding and cage plates.

components.name: Seam sealer
components.description: Flexible sealer applied over all stitch-welded and disturbed seams after priming to keep water and fumes out and to stop crevice corrosion.

components.description: Epoxy primer over all bare/welded metal followed by a durable topcoat (cockpit often painted light grey/white so leaks and cracks are easy to see). Use weld-through primer on mating faces before welding plates.
components.location: Entire shell interior, engine bay and underbody.

raceOptions.name: 2K epoxy primer + 2K urethane topcoat
raceOptions.notes: Light colour in cockpit aids inspection.

fluids.name: Epoxy primer
fluids.spec: 2K epoxy

Leave bare-metal ground pads for electrical grounds (see electrical.grounding).

components.name: Cavity wax / internal rust proofing
components.description: Penetrating wax sprayed into rails, rockers and pillars after welding (welding burns off internal factory e-coat). Apply after paint, with long-wand nozzles through existing access holes.
components.location: Inside rockers, front and rear rails, pillars.

raceOptions.name: Cavity wax
raceOptions.brand: 3M Cavity Wax Plus, Eastwood Internal Frame Coating, Bilt Hamber Dynax

installNotes: Apply after all welding, before installing harnesses/lines in those cavities.

components.name: Underbody stone-chip coating

raceOptions.name: Paintable chip guard / raptor-type liner (thin coat)

installNotes: Mask lift points, datum holes and all threaded holes.

components.name: Transmission / driveshaft tunnel
components.description: Raised center section of the floor that houses the TR-6060 (or 10L90) transmission tail, the driveshaft and the dual exhaust. It is a key torsional member. Race builds may need local clearancing for larger exhaust, a dry-sump-related engine setback, or a sequential/transaxle swap; any cut must be boxed back in to restore stiffness.
components.location: Car centerline, x approx 0.7-2.6, y approx 0.18-0.45.

raceOptions.name: Clearanced and re-boxed tunnel (fabricated)

Maintain at least 25 mm (1 in) between exhaust and the tunnel/fuel or brake lines, or add heat shielding.

factory.name: GM factory tunnel brace
