components.name: Rear tow point
components.description: Rear tow eye receptacle / rear tow strap mounted to the rear rail or rear bumper beam. Must be reachable without removing bodywork and must clear the diffuser and exhaust.
components.location: Rear fascia lower area, x approx 3.80, y approx 0.35.

factory.name: GM rear tow eye receptacle (screw-in eye)

raceOptions.name: Bolt-on nylon tow strap

hardware.spec: M10 or M12 flange bolt with fender washer (match receptacle)

inspection: Check strap condition each event.

modelRef.features: Threaded tow point with tow strap

components.name: Rivnuts / nutserts for line, harness and bracket mounting
components.description: Steel threaded insert rivets installed into body sheet metal to give removable mounting points for brake/fuel line clamps, harness P-clips, fire-system lines, ducting, splash shields and panels without access to the back side. Use steel (not aluminum) rivnuts in structural or vibrating locations; avoid installing them in rail walls, datum holes or crush zones.
components.location: Throughout: tunnel and floor (line runs), firewall, inner fenders, trunk floor.

factory.name: Factory weld studs and clip holes (partially reusable)
factory.notes: Many factory line clips snap onto weld studs; reuse where routing matches.

raceOptions.name: Steel ribbed rivnuts M5/M6 (or 10-24 / 1/4-20)
raceOptions.notes: Hex-body rivnuts resist spinning better than round-body in thin sheet.

specs.Typical sizes: M5 and M6 in 0.7-1.5 mm sheet
specs.Install: Hand or pneumatic rivnut tool, correct grip range

hardware.item: Screw into M6 steel rivnut (P-clip/line clamp)
hardware.notes: Per fastener; over-torque spins the rivnut.

installNotes: Lay out every line and harness route (phase 2/8) and mark clip positions every 300-400 mm before drilling.
Drill to exact rivnut size, deburr, prime the bare edge (weld-thru or epoxy primer) before setting the rivnut to stop rust.
Install before final paint if possible, then mask threads.
inspection: Check for spinning rivnuts on high-vibration items (exhaust hangers, splash shields).

modelRef.features: Ribbed steel rivnuts

components.name: Weld-on tabs and brackets (line clamps, harness, fire system, ducts)
components.description: Small steel tabs (often with a weld nut) MIG/TIG welded to the body or cage for line clamps, harness clamps, extinguisher mounts, brake-duct hose supports and splitter/diffuser supports. Welding them on during chassis prep (before paint) is cleaner than rivnuts in many locations.
components.location: Tunnel, firewall, inner fenders, cage tubes.

raceOptions.name: Laser-cut steel tabs with captured weld nuts

installNotes: Weld all tabs before media-blasting/painting; tabs welded after paint must be re-primed.
inspection: Check tab welds for cracking.

components.name: Captured (cage) nut plates for cradle and brace bolts
components.description: The cradle and cradle-brace bolts thread into captured/caged weld nuts in the rails. A spun or stripped captured nut is a common problem on used shells. Repair by cutting an access window, welding in a new nut plate (or installing a threaded insert of equal strength), and closing the window with a doubler.
components.location: Front rails at front cradle mounts; rear rails at rear cradle mounts and cradle braces.

factory.name: GM captured weld nuts
factory.notes: Cradle bolts are torque-to-yield (74 lb ft + 90-105 deg on the rear cradle), so thread condition matters.

raceOptions.name: Weld-in nut plate / heavy-duty thread insert (e.g. Time-Sert)
raceOptions.notes: Thread repair inserts must be rated for the TTY clamp load.

installNotes: Thread-chase every captured nut before assembly; test-fit each bolt by hand to full depth.

sources.title: BMR BK061 instructions (rear cradle TAY bolts)

components.name: Front structure stitch welds (rails, aprons, strut towers, dash)
components.description: Short MIG stitch welds added between factory spot welds along the front rail flanges, the strut-tower-to-apron seams, the tower-to-rail joint and the dash-to-tower junction. This prevents spot-weld peel and seam slip under racing loads and raises torsional stiffness, especially at the front where the Gen 6 strut towers carry the full front spring/damper load.
components.location: Engine bay: front rails, strut towers (x approx -0.1 to 0.2, y 0.5-0.85, z +/-0.5), dash/cowl junction.

factory.name: Factory spot welds + structural adhesive
factory.notes: GM uses spot welds and structural adhesive. Adhesive and sealer must be ground/burned away locally before stitch welding (fumes are toxic; ventilate and wear a respirator).

raceOptions.name: Stitch weld pattern: 25 mm (1 in) bead every 50-75 mm, alternating sides
raceOptions.notes: Short, cool stitches minimize heat distortion and burn-through of thin (0.7-1.2 mm) sheet. Fully continuous seams are not necessary and add distortion/weight.

specs.Prep: Strip seam sealer, adhesive and e-coat to bright metal 10 mm each side

installNotes: Measure the shell (cradle mount diagonals, tower-to-tower) before welding and fixture/brace the body so it cannot move.
Strip sealer and paint along each seam with a wire wheel / stripping disc; remove adhesive with heat gun and scraper.
Weld in a skip pattern, alternating side-to-side and front-to-rear to spread heat; let areas cool before continuing.
Re-measure, then re-seal seams with seam sealer and prime (see chassis.corrosion-and-coatings).
inspection: Inspect weld toes at strut towers for cracking after first race weekend and every few events thereafter.

modelRef.features: 25 mm MIG stitches along the tower/apron seams

components.name: Underbody stitch welds (floor-to-rocker, tunnel, seat cross-members)
components.description: Stitch welds along the floor-to-rocker seam, floor-to-tunnel seams and seat cross-member flanges, done mostly from inside the cockpit with the interior stripped. These seams carry the main torsional shear path between front and rear structures.
components.location: Cockpit floor, x approx 0.75-2.6.

specs.Process: MIG stitch, same parameters as front structure

installNotes: Remove all deadener first (dry ice or heat gun + scraper).
Remove fuel and brake lines from the underside before welding near them, or shield them; route new lines after welding (phase 2).
inspection: Check for cracking near cage feet and seat mounts.

modelRef.features: MIG stitch beads

components.name: Rear structure stitch welds (rear rails, shock towers, wheelhouses)
components.description: Stitch welds at the rear rail flanges, rear wheelhouse-to-shock-tower seams and the rear floor kick-up. The rear cradle bushings and braces feed tractive and cornering loads into this area.
components.location: Rear wheelhouses and trunk, x approx 2.4-3.3.
installNotes: Remove fuel tank, rear cradle and all trim from the rear area before welding.
inspection: Check rear cradle mount areas for cracking.

modelRef.features: MIG stitch beads

components.name: Cradle mount reinforcement plates (front and rear)
components.description: Steel doubler/spreader plates welded around the front and rear cradle mounting points on the rails. Recommended when the cradles are solid-mounted (rubber isolators removed), because the body then sees sharper load peaks at these 8 points.
components.location: Front cradle mounts approx (x -0.38 and 0.12, y 0.30, z +/-0.42); rear cradle mounts approx (x 2.45 and 3.08, y 0.40, z +/-0.48).

factory.name: None (factory relies on rail section and captured nut plate)

raceOptions.name: Fabricated 3-4 mm (0.120-0.160 in) steel doubler plates
raceOptions.notes: Plug weld + perimeter stitch; keep the captured-nut bore concentric and do not distort the nut plate.

installNotes: Install the cradle loosely (with bolts) before welding the plates to keep holes aligned; remove cradle before final welding.
inspection: Check for cracking at plate perimeters.

GM Gen 6 Camaro rear suspension exploded diagram: 5 links, knuckle with 3 bushings, shock, spring, stabilizer, cradle with 4 mounts

modelRef.features: Doublers around each cradle bolt on the body rails

components.name: Strut tower reinforcement / gussets
components.description: Plates or gussets welded to the inside of the front strut towers and between tower and rail/apron, and a reinforcing ring around the top-mount area. Especially important with camber plates (load is offset) and with hard-mounted race top mounts.
components.location: Front strut towers, x approx 0.05, y 0.6-0.85, z +/-0.55.

raceOptions.name: Fabricated tower top doubler with cage tie-in tab
raceOptions.notes: Keep 3-bolt top-mount pattern and the camber-plate slot clear.

installNotes: Trial-fit camber plates and strut tower brace before welding reinforcement so bolt holes and clearances are maintained.
inspection: Look for cracks around the top-mount bolt holes.

modelRef.features: Tower-top doubler with centre hole and 3 stud holes

components.name: Roll-cage mounting / backing plates (body interface)
components.description: Steel landing plates welded to floor, rockers, A/B pillars and rear shock towers to receive the cage feet. The plates spread cage loads into the unibody. Sizes and thickness are set by the governing rulebook (NASA CCR / SCCA GCR cage rules specify minimum plate area and thickness).
components.location: Main hoop feet near B-pillar (x approx 2.1, z +/-0.75), front hoop/A-pillar feet (x approx 0.85), rear down-bar feet at rear shock towers (x approx 2.75).

raceOptions.name: Plates per rulebook (typically >= 0.080-0.125 in steel, >= 16-36 sq in depending on rules)
raceOptions.notes: Confirm exact minimums in the current NASA CCR / SCCA GCR before cutting plates.

installNotes: Owned jointly with the safety system; welded during chassis prep (phase 1) before paint.
inspection: Check plate welds during annual tech.

modelRef.features: Cage backing plates with hole

components.name: Front strut tower brace
components.description: Cross-car bar bolted to the three strut top-mount bolt locations on each tower, reducing tower-to-tower flex and keeping front camber consistent under load. On the Gen 6 V8 cars the bar must clear the LT1 intake or LT4 supercharger lid. If a cage with forward tubes to the towers is fitted, the brace becomes largely redundant.
components.location: Across the engine bay at the tower tops, x approx 0.05, y approx 0.87, z from +0.55 to -0.55.

factory.name: Not fitted on most Gen 6 trims
factory.notes: Verify for your car; several trims have no factory bar.

raceOptions.name: BMR STB018 front strut tower brace (V8 only)
raceOptions.notes: Replaces all 6 strut tower bolts with supplied longer bolts and spacers, torque 16 ft-lb. Does not fit V6/2.0T. If using BMR WAK360/361 camber plates use the longer plate bolts supplied for the brace.

raceOptions.name: Cage forward tubes to towers (if class allows)
raceOptions.notes: Stiffer than any bolt-on brace.

hardware.item: Strut tower brace bolt (replaces strut upper mounting bolt)
hardware.spec: M8 long flange bolt + spacer (supplied with brace), 13 mm hex
hardware.torqueSequence: Wheels on ground or strut supported so it cannot drop; snug all, then torque
hardware.notes: Discard the factory bolts per BMR; same torque as GM strut upper mounting bolt.

installNotes: Install with the car on its wheels (or the knuckles supported) so the struts do not drop out of the locator holes when bolts are removed.
Install after camber plates and after the engine (supercharger/intake clearance).
inspection: Re-torque bolts after first session; check for contact with intake/supercharger under engine rock.

modelRef.features: Tube brace with 3-stud end plates on the strut tops, arched over the engine

components.name: Rear shock tower brace / trunk cross-brace
components.description: Cross-car brace between the rear shock towers (trunk side) or cage rear down-tube cross bar. Stiffens the rear damper mounts, which matters more if the car is converted to rear coilovers that put spring load into the shock pad.
components.location: Trunk, x approx 2.75, y approx 0.72, z +/-0.58.

raceOptions.name: Fabricated tubular bar or cage cross tube

hardware.notes: Generic for a fabricated bolt-on brace; do not reuse the factory shock nuts as brace fasteners unless the brace was designed for them (factory shock nuts are 43 N·m).

installNotes: Fit after rear shocks/coilovers so top mount clearance can be checked.

modelRef.features: Fabricated tube between the rear shock tower tops

components.name: Body-in-white shell (bare unibody)
components.description: Complete welded steel monocoque of the 2016-2024 Camaro coupe. GM states the Gen 6 structure is 28% stiffer in torsion and 133 lb (60.5 kg) lighter than the Gen 5 body, largely through more high-strength steel and an aluminum instrument-panel frame. For a race build it is the reference for every hard point; it should be put on a rotisserie or measuring jig, stripped to bare metal in critical areas, and checked against GM body dimension charts before any welding.
components.location: Whole car, front bumper beam (x approx -0.95) to rear panel (x approx 3.8).

factory.name: GM Gen 6 Camaro coupe body structure (Alpha architecture, Lansing Grand River)
factory.notes: Steel unibody with bolt-on aluminum hood and front fenders (body system). Coupe is far stiffer than the convertible; always start a road-race build from a coupe shell. ZL1/ZL1 1LE and SS share the body-in-white; ZL1 adds unique fascia, cooling openings and cradle/brace details.

raceOptions.name: Seam/stitch-welded and cage-integrated shell
raceOptions.notes: Most effective stiffness upgrade: stitch weld critical seams and tie a multi-point cage into strut towers, A/B pillars, rockers and rear shock towers (see chassis.seam-welding-and-reinforcement and safety.roll-cage).

specs.Track (ZL1): Front 63.4 in / 1610 mm; rear 62.6 in / 1591 mm
specs.Curb weight reference: ZL1 coupe manual 3883 lb; ZL1 1LE approx 3820 lb (GM est.)

installNotes: Mount the shell on a rotisserie or a bench jig using the cradle mounting points so the body is supported on its own hard points and does not sag while stripped.

Measure all front and rear cradle mounting holes, strut tower top-mount holes and rear shock tower holes against GM body dimension data (corner-to-corner diagonals). Record the numbers before welding; re-measure after welding.
Remove all sealers, deadener and undercoating only where welding or cage plates will go; keep the factory e-coat elsewhere to preserve corrosion protection.
Plug or document every unused hole; keep the factory locating holes (datum holes) open - they are needed for measuring and for refitting cradles.
inspection: Check for cracked spot welds and paint cracking at strut towers, front rail kick-ups, rocker-to-floor joints and rear shock towers after every few events.
Re-measure cradle-mount diagonals after any off-track excursion or impact.

components.name: Front frame rails (longitudinal members) and lower load path
components.description: Closed-section steel rails running from the front bumper beam back under the dash to the floor. The front cradle bolts up into captured nuts in these rails, and the engine/front suspension loads pass through them into the rockers and tunnel. Their kick-up under the toe board is a common crack/buckle location on hard-driven cars.
components.location: Engine bay, both sides of engine, x approx -0.9 to 0.65, y approx 0.35-0.55, z approx +/-0.42.

factory.name: GM stamped/welded high-strength steel front rails with crush zones
factory.notes: Front crush cans/bumper beam bolt to the rail tips. Do not drill or notch the rails for line routing; use rivnuts on non-structural flanges.

raceOptions.name: Stitch-welded rails with gusseted kick-up and cage tie-in bars to strut towers
raceOptions.notes: Commonly done in conjunction with a cage that extends forward through the firewall (if allowed by class rules).

specs.Front cradle attachment: Bolts into captured weld nuts in rail (verify thread)

installNotes: Chase all captured cradle nuts with a thread chaser (not a cutting tap) and blow out debris before the cradle goes in.
If cage tubes are run forward to the rails/towers, use spreader plates and weld to clean bare metal.
inspection: Inspect rail kick-ups below the dash and rail-to-tower junctions for paint cracking or buckling.
Check captured nuts for spinning or pulled threads whenever cradle bolts are serviced.

modelRef.features: Straight front rails (Alpha: suspension bolts to straight rails) kicking down under the dash to the floor; carry the front cradle mounts

components.name: Front strut towers (shock towers)
components.description: Stamped steel towers that take the full vertical load of the front MacPherson struts through three top-mount bolts per side (plus the strut rod on ZL1 1LE hard-mounted DSSV top mounts). They are the primary target for seam welding, gusseting, strut-tower bracing and cage tie-ins.
components.location: Engine bay corners, top at x approx 0.05, y approx 0.85, z approx +/-0.55.

factory.name: GM stamped steel strut tower with 3-bolt top mount pattern
factory.notes: Factory top mount fastens with 3 bolts (13 mm head) per side; ZL1 1LE DSSV top mounts are hard mounted (no rubber isolation) and can be rotated 180 deg for more negative camber.

raceOptions.name: Caster/camber plates (BMR WAK360 for OE springs, WAK361 for coilovers)
raceOptions.notes: Uses an aluminum spacer bracket bolted into the tower; adds approx 2.5 deg total camber range plus caster adjustment.

specs.Top mount fasteners: 3 bolts per side (13 mm hex), 22 N·m (16 lb ft)
specs.Tower top: approx 850 mm above ground at race ride height

hardware.item: Strut upper mounting bolt (strut mount to tower)
hardware.spec: M8 class flange bolt, 13 mm hex (thread size inferred from 13 mm head)
hardware.torqueSequence: Install all three loosely, install strut-to-knuckle fasteners, then torque the three upper bolts
hardware.notes: Per side. BMR STB018 strut-tower brace replaces these with longer bolts at the same 16 ft-lb.

installNotes: Seam weld the tower-to-apron and tower-to-rail seams (see chassis.seam-welding-and-reinforcement.strut-tower-gussets).
Clean paint off the top-mount landing face only if a camber plate spacer requires metal contact; otherwise keep it coated.
Check that strut top-mount holes are round and undamaged; elongated holes indicate the strut has been moving and must be repaired before alignment.
inspection: Look for cracking radiating from the three bolt holes and the center hole.
Re-torque top-mount bolts after the first shakedown.

components.name: Dash panel (firewall), cowl and plenum
components.description: Steel bulkhead separating engine bay and cockpit plus the cowl box under the windshield. Ties the strut towers and A-pillars together and carries the steering column support and pedal box. Pass-throughs for the intermediate steering shaft, brake lines, harnesses and (in race builds) fuel and cooling lines must be grommeted and sealed.
components.location: x approx 0.60-0.70, y approx 0.25-0.95, full width.

factory.name: GM dash panel with sound insulation, cowl/plenum with wiper module
factory.notes: The factory instrument panel frame (cross-car beam) is aluminum on Gen 6 (saves 9.2 lb per GM); it carries the column. In a race build the IP beam is often replaced by a steel dash bar in the cage.

raceOptions.name: Cage dash bar with fabricated column mount
raceOptions.notes: Required if the factory IP beam is removed; design column mount to hold factory column or a race column (steering.column-and-shaft.column).

specs.Material: Steel dash panel; aluminum IP cross-car beam (factory)

installNotes: Remove all factory deadener from the cockpit side before seam sealing/painting.
Plan every firewall pass-through before painting: bulkhead connectors for harness, bulkhead fittings for fuel/brake/oil lines, and the I-shaft boot.
inspection: Check pass-through grommets for chafing and heat damage (exhaust headers run close on the driver side).

components.name: Rocker panels (sills)
components.description: Closed-section longitudinal members along each side of the floor that carry most of the bending and torsional load between front and rear structures. Factory lift/jack points are on the rocker pinch welds. Cage main-hoop and door-bar feet usually land on or next to the rockers.

factory.name: GM steel rocker inner/outer with pinch-weld flange
factory.notes: Outer rocker cover is a plastic body panel on Gen 6 (body system).

installNotes: Stitch weld the rocker-to-floor seam from inside the cockpit where accessible.
Use a slotted rubber pinch-weld adapter on jacks/stands; never lift on the plastic rocker cover.
inspection: Check pinch weld flanges for crush damage from jacks.

components.description: Stamped steel front and rear floor sections with seat cross-members, welded to the rockers and the transmission/driveshaft tunnel. components.location: Cockpit floor, x approx 0.75-2.6, y approx 0.15-0.18.

factory.name: GM steel floor pan with seat cross members
factory.notes: Contains several body plugs/drain holes (see chassis.floor-and-tunnel.body-plugs-and-grommets).

specs.Underside height: approx 150-180 mm at race ride height

installNotes: Mark and remove unused factory brackets (carpet studs, console brackets) only after the cage and seat layout is final.

components.name: A/B/C pillars, roof rails and roof bows
components.description: Upper body ring that closes the torsion box. Cage tubes run close to the A-pillars, B-pillars and roof rails and are typically welded to them via plates (where class rules allow) to dramatically increase torsional stiffness.
components.location: A-pillar base x approx 0.70, B-pillar x approx 2.15, roof y approx 1.36, x approx 1.2-2.6.

factory.name: GM high-strength steel pillars and roof rails
factory.notes: Coupe roof; convertible lacks this ring and is unsuitable for racing.

installNotes: Remove headliner, pillar trims and curtain airbags (disable the SRS system first) before cage fitting.
inspection: Inspect cage-to-pillar welds and plates.

factory.name: GM steel rear rails with captured nuts for rear cradle and braces

components.description: Rear floor pan aft of the rear cradle including the spare-tire area. In road-race builds this is typically cut and replaced with a flat panel or a fuel-cell well/mounting frame, and it carries the fuel cell, battery box or ballast mounts.

components.name: Body datum / locating holes (measurement reference)
components.description: Factory gauge holes and cradle locating holes used by the body shop and assembly plant to locate the cradles and to measure the body. They are the reference for setting up a jig, measuring after welding, and re-installing cradles in the exact factory position (important because front caster and rear toe/camber depend on cradle position).
components.location: Underside: front rails near cradle mounts, rocker pinch welds, rear rails near rear cradle mounts.

factory.name: GM body dimension reference holes
factory.notes: Obtain body dimension (underbody) charts from GM service information (Body Repair - Underbody Dimensions).

installNotes: Never weld over or enlarge datum holes; mask them during undercoating removal and painting.
inspection: Use them for post-crash measurement.

components.name: Main hoop (B-pillar hoop)
components.description: Single-piece, near-vertical hoop immediately behind the front seats that carries roll-over loads to the floor. It is the backbone of the cage: the harness bar, main-hoop diagonal, backstays, roof rails and door bars all terminate on it. Must be one continuous bent tube (no joints) with the near-vertical legs as close as possible to the B-pillar inner panels and only one bend in each leg.
components.location: Spans the cabin at the B-pillar, x ≈ 2.15–2.18; feet welded to plates on the floor/rocker junction (z ≈ ±0.66), top tucked under the roof skin at y ≈ 1.27.

factory.name: None – production Camaro has no roll structure (CMS Performance offers a Gen 6 bolt-in roll bar as a street/HPDE step)

raceOptions.name: Custom weld-in cage, 1.75 x .120 DOM (NASA 3,001–4,000 lb bracket)
raceOptions.brand: Local chassis shop / S&W Race Cars / Autopower (custom)
raceOptions.notes: Gen 6 race weight w/o driver & fuel ≈ 3,400–3,700 lb → 1.75 x .120 per NASA CCR table quoted in the sources; SCCA 2,700 lb+ allows 1.50 x .120 / 1.75 x .095 / 2.00 x .080.

raceOptions.name: Chromoly 4130 1.75 x .095 or .120 (normalized)
raceOptions.notes: Lighter; requires TIG and qualified welder; SCCA forbids mixing alloy and mild tube in one cage.

raceOptions.name: FIA build-to-spec main hoop 45 x 2.5 mm or 50 x 2.0 mm (350 N/mm² min)
raceOptions.notes: For FIA-style events; note post-2017 homologated cars must use homologated/certified cages.

specs.Tube: 1.750 in OD x 0.120 in wall DOM (SAE 1020/1026) or 4130 seamless
specs.Helmet clearance: SCCA: ≥ 2 in above helmet (cars w/o roof); NASA: pad within reach of helmet

hardware.item: TIG/MIG weld joint – full 360° fillet, full penetration
hardware.spec: ER70S-2/ER70S-6 (mild/DOM) or ER80S-D2 / ER70S-2 per 4130 practice
hardware.notes: FIA 253-8.3.4: all welds full penetration around the whole tube perimeter, preferably gas-shielded arc. Do not mix mild and alloy tube (SCCA).

hardware.spec: 3/16–1/4 in drilled hole in non-critical straight section
hardware.notes: SCCA requires an inspection hole in front and main hoops and one supplemental brace (or non-invasive ultrasonic measurement logged in the logbook).

installNotes: Strip cabin to bare metal (interior.strip-and-deadener-removal) and seam-weld if planned before fitting tubes.
Fit seat, steering column and pedal box mock-up first so the hoop clears the driver helmet with the seat in final position.
Tack mounting plates, then notch-fit the hoop through the roof line as high and close to the B-pillar as possible.
Check driver helmet clearance with driver seated + helmet + FHR before final welding.
Final-weld in alternating short beads to minimize distortion; weld plates 360°.
Drill inspection hole per SCCA, mark with paint pen, record wall thickness in logbook.
inspection: Check all welds for cracks (dye-penetrant after any impact).
Inspect foot plates and surrounding floor for cracking/tearing.
Verify padding still secured where helmet can contact.

components.description: Steel plates welded to the floor/rocker junction under each main-hoop leg. They spread roll-over load into the unibody and give the tube a 360° weld land. Often bent to wrap up the rocker inner wall (multi-plane plates are allowed).

specs.NASA size: 9–100 in² each, each side 2–12 in, ≥ 0.080 in if welded (CCR 15.6.14 as quoted)

hardware.spec: MIG/TIG stitch then continuous perimeter weld to floor/rocker

hardware.spec: 3/8-16 UNC hex bolt + nyloc + hardened washers, through backing plate of equal size/thickness
hardware.notes: SCCA L3 bolted plates need backing plate of equal size & thickness, ≥ 3 bolts typical; FIA requires ≥ 3 × M8 8.8 per foot on a 3 mm/120 cm² reinforcement plate (M8 8.8 ≈ 25 N·m). installNotes: Grind e-coat/sealer to bare metal; plates should sit flat with full contact.
Weld plates to chassis before final tube weld so the tube can be welded 360° to the plate.
Avoid placing plates over seam-sealed joints without first welding the seam.
inspection: Check for floor cracking around plate edges.

components.description: Sequence: farthest from the master first – RR, LR, RF, LF; on each Brembo/AP caliper bleed the INNER bleeder first, then OUTER. Keep reservoirs full throughout. components.name: Pad & rotor bedding procedure (system service item)
components.description: Lays an even transfer film of pad material on the rotor; skipping it causes judder and inconsistent bite. Generic procedure (follow pad maker if different): several moderate on/off applications building heat up to ~65 mph, then 8–10 firm stops from 55–65 mph down to ~25 mph without stopping fully, then a cool-down lap/drive without using the brakes, and let the brakes return to ambient before racing.
components.location: On track / test road.

raceOptions.name: Pre-bedded discs/pads (Essex offers a $100 disc burnishing service with kit purchase)

installNotes: Never hold the car stationary on the brakes immediately after bedding (pad imprint on hot rotor).
inspection: Even grey transfer film across the rotor face indicates good bedding.

Do NOT use the 60 N·m+90° / 40 N·m+90° values seen online – those are for base-car (JL9) caliper brackets. [2026-10 check] The final angle is now filled in. A camaro6.com owner quotes the GM SI (2019 SS Brembo) as 150 N·m + 15–30°. TightTorque (GM 2016–18 SI) gives 150 N·m first pass for J55/J6G, and an ATS (Alpha) owner quotes 150 N·m + 30°. installNotes: Install hub bearing, dust shield/duct backing plate and rotor first.
Clean knuckle threads; apply blue threadlocker to new bolts; torque 150 N·m then turn +15–30°.
Confirm caliper orientation: bleeders must be at the TOP (left and right calipers are handed – swapping sides puts bleeders at the bottom and you cannot bleed air out).
Fit pads, pins, spring and cross bolt; connect hose with new crush washers.
Spin the hub: rotor must not touch the caliper bridge; check radial clearance to the wheel spokes with the race wheel (≥ 3 mm).
inspection: Every session: look for fluid at pistons/boots and bleeders; check pad thickness through the caliper window.
Every event: check caliper bolt torque marks; inspect dust boots (factory) for heat damage; temperature paint on the caliper body (aim < ~200 °C caliper body).
Every season: rebuild seals (factory kit: 2x30/34/38 mm seals and boots per caliper).

Bed new rotors/pads before racing (see brakes.fluid.bedding-procedure).
inspection: Measure thickness at 4 points every event; replace at the manufacturer minimum (stamped on hat/ring) or ~2 mm worn for race discs.
Look for heat-check cracks: small surface crazing OK; any crack reaching the OD edge or into a vane – replace immediately.
Check for uneven pad deposits (vibration) and blueing.

installNotes: Strip the block completely, remove every galley plug (including the barbell plug) and hot-tank/ultrasonic clean the oil passages.

Chase every threaded hole: head bolt holes M12x1.75 (ARP 912-0008 / 912-0016) and M8x1.25 (ARP 912-0001). The factory head-bolt threads carry thread-locking compound that must be removed or new fasteners can stretch/break before final torque.
If converting to ARP main studs, align hone the mains with the studs torqued to final preload with Ultra-Torque lube (ARP instruction footnote).
Bore/hone with a deck (torque) plate installed using the same head fasteners and torque that will be used in final assembly.
Check deck flatness and cylinder wall finish; measure every main and cam bore before buying bearings.
Install all cup/galley plugs, oil squirters and cam bearings before the crank goes in.
inspection: At teardown: check liner walls for scuffing/cracks at the top of the bore, check main-cap fretting, check for coolant in oil.
Leak-down test between race weekends (<10% typical healthy race engine).

Torque in sequence in the passes listed in hardware; M8 corner fasteners last.

hardware.torqueSequence: Magnuson 10-bolt pattern (5 per head flange), center-out alternating sides: 1 = left/driver center, 2 = right center, 3 = left rear-center, 4 = right front-center, 5 = left front-center, 6 = right rear-center, 7 = left rearmost, 8 = right frontmost, 9 = left frontmost, 10 = right rearmost (read from Magnuson top-view diagram with pulley/front at left - verify against your manual).

Remains typical.

Gradually work up to final; pulley must still spin freely.
Cross pattern 1-2-3-4 (top, bottom, left, right).

installNotes: Clean head flanges; install all 8 port gaskets (engine.intake-manifold.port-gaskets) and the PCV seal at the bottom of the housing (lube with Super Lube).

Torque in sequence gradually; confirm pulley spins freely afterwards.
Vacuum leak-down test the intercooler circuit before adding coolant (Magnuson).
inspection: Check SC oil level/condition per manufacturer (Eaton TVS units are sealed for life on OEM; aftermarket may differ).
Inspect coupler/isolator noise, belt alignment, bypass operation.

components.name: Dry-sump oil pan (billet, Gen V LT)
components.description: Shallow billet-aluminum pan that replaces the wet sump. Scavenge pickups (one per section / crank bay pair) pull oil out of the crankcase as fast as it drains so the crank never windages through oil, and the shallow depth allows a lower engine position. installNotes: Remove old bearing with a slide-hammer puller (or the bread/grease hydraulic trick); never gouge the crank bore.
Clean bore, check for spun-bearing scoring.
Press new bearing in with a correctly-sized driver on the OUTER race only, seal facing the transmission, flush or to the depth specified by GM/clutch maker.
Confirm input shaft pilot slides in freely (test with the clutch alignment tool).
inspection: Spin by finger - no roughness or grease weep
Check input-shaft pilot for bluing/wear when trans is out

hardware.torque: 11 ft-lb (15 N·m), then 22 ft-lb (30 N·m), then +45°
hardware.torqueSequence: Three passes in a criss-cross sequence: 15 N·m, then 30 N·m, then a final +45° angle. Use NEW GM bolts (torque-to-angle, one-time use).

The 2016-18 Camaro SM (via TightTorque, 15/30 N·m), Summit SR-05493 and Rated R agree. CORRECTED from 20/50/100 N·m, which was the Gen III/IV (LS) torque-only procedure.

Checked 2026-10: the ARP instruction sheet for 234-2801 (Chevy Gen V 6.2L LT1 flywheel bolt, the 1.125 in UHL sister part) specifies 85 ft-lb with Loctite 242 on the threads and Ultra-Torque under the head, no washers, and a chamfered flywheel. components.name: Rear differential assembly (226 mm, eLSD)
components.description: Aluminum-cased independent-rear-suspension differential carried in the rear cradle on three bushings (two front, one rear). ZL1/1LE cars use a 226 mm unit with a GM electronic limited-slip differential (eLSD): a hydraulically actuated clutch pack that varies locking between 0 and 2,000 N·m (1,475 lb-ft) breakaway torque and reaches full engagement within 0.150 s, integrated with Performance Traction Management. Ratio 3.73:1 with the manual transmission.

factory.name: GM 226 mm rear drive module with eLSD (ZL1 / ZL1 1LE / SS 1LE)
factory.notes: eLSD (RPO G96) on 2017+ ZL1 and SS 1LE, 2018+ ZL1 1LE (as quoted from GM). Final drive 3.73 (manual), 2.85 (ZL1 10-speed auto). Rear axle needs 1,500 mi (2,400 km) break-in before track use; standard rear diff cooler on ZL1 1LE. The eLSD is controlled through the GM vehicle network - with a non-GM race ECU/chassis electronics it will not be commanded correctly, which is the main reason race builds convert to a mechanical LSD.

components.name: Transmission (TREMEC TR-6060 / race gearbox)
components.description: Six-speed manual gearbox behind the bellhousing. The factory Gen 6 manual is the TREMEC 6060 (TR-6060): aluminum case, triple-cone synchros on 1st/2nd, double-cone on 3rd-6th and reverse, tapered roller bearings on main and countershaft, internal shift rails with an external shift rod to a rearward-mounted shifter, solenoid 2nd/3rd inhibit (skip-shift) and reverse inhibit; rated 650 lb-ft (881 N·m) input. Race alternatives are a TREMEC Magnum XL (stronger H-pattern), a dog-ring conversion, or a sequential dog box (Holinger RD6, Xtrac as on the Camaro GT4.R, Samsonas).
components.location: In the transmission tunnel from bellhousing (x≈0.56) to output flange (x≈1.25), centerline y≈0.36-0.40, z=0.

factory.name: TREMEC 6060 6-speed manual, RPO MH3 (ZL1 1LE)

Final drive 3.73 with manual (ZL1).

raceOptions.name: TREMEC Magnum XL (GM) close-ratio

installNotes: Fill with fluid before installation (easier on the bench) - or plan access to the fill plug in the car.

components.name: Alternator field-kill relay / dump resistor
components.description: When the master switch opens with the engine running, the alternator can keep the ignition/ECU alive (engine run-on) and voltage can spike. A power resistor across the alternator output (switched in by the master switch's aux pole) or a field-kill relay that drops the alternator L/field terminal ensures the engine stops. With the Gen V LT ECM-controlled alternator, killing the ECM run feed also drops the L-terminal command.
components.location: Near the master switch or on the firewall, on a heat-tolerant aluminum mount.

installNotes: Mount on bare metal for heat sinking; insulate the terminals.

A race build moves to a standalone that logs and tunes freely – but must support GDI, which narrows the choice.

Typical channel plan on this car: ECU main, ignition coils, injectors/DI driver, fuel pumps (2 x PWM), radiator fan (PWM), intercooler pump, starter, dash/logger, keypad, ABS, alternator L-terminal, rain light, brake lights, headlights, wipers, radio, camera, cool-suit, transponder (if not always-hot), data sensors 12 V.
components.location: Passenger side under/behind the dash on a vibration-isolated aluminum panel (x≈1.05, y≈0.55, z≈-0.40), close to the ECU and the firewall bulkhead.

factory.name: GM underhood fuse block (X50A) + rear fuse block (X51) + BCM-switched relays
factory.notes: Factory blocks are tied to the BCM/body harness; with a standalone ECU and stripped body harness they are removed.

raceOptions.name: MoTeC PDM30
raceOptions.notes: 8 x 20 A + 22 x 8 A outputs (115 A / 60 A transient), 16 switch inputs, 1 CAN, M6 battery stud, 34 + 26 pin connectors, 270–300 g. Config via PDM Manager + UTC #61059.

raceOptions.name: AiM PDM32
raceOptions.notes: 28 high-side outputs (4 x 20 A, 12 x 15 A, 12 x 10 A) + 4 x 35 A half-bridge, 120 A total, 14 inputs, 3 CAN + LIN; built-in logger/dash controller with 6 or 10 in display.

raceOptions.name: ECUMaster PMU16
raceOptions.notes: 10 x 25 A + 6 x 15 A, 150 A total, 16 analog inputs, 2 CAN, wiper H-bridge, IMU; DL version logs 256 MB. Strong value option.

raceOptions.name: Cartek Power Distribution Panel PDP-16
raceOptions.notes: 16 outputs with built-in push-button panel (no laptop needed), 5/10/15 A selectable, 160 A total, 16 ECU inputs, wiper module, AMPSEAL connectors. No CAN keypad needed.

hardware.spec: M6 x 1.0 nut + spring washer on ring lug
hardware.notes: MoTeC specifies an M6 stud; torque value not found – do not over-torque the PCB-mounted stud. Support the cable with a P-clamp so its weight is not on the stud.

hardware.spec: M5 screws through rubber isolators into rivnuts
M5 rubber bobbin isolators (~30 Shore A–50 Shore A)

installNotes: Write the load list with continuous/inrush currents first; assign 20 A channels to fans, pumps, starter and ignition; pair outputs where current exceeds a channel rating.
Mount the PDM within ~1 m of the battery-feed junction with the main cable fused.
Program soft-start/PWM for fan and fuel pumps; program retries (e.g. 3) except for the starter.
Program logic: engine-kill input from isolator → all engine outputs off; rain light ON with headlights or keypad; brake lights from brake-pressure channel via CAN.
Log every output current; set warning thresholds on the dash.
inspection: Review PDM fault/trip log after each session.
Connector locks/seals; mounting isolators.
